item.title: Bangladesh prepares to extract gas from Inani
item.description:
Bangladesh has started preparations to extract natural gas from Inani in Ukhiya upazila of Cox’s Bazar, where a gas-fuelled fire has been burning for 18 days following a deep tube-well drilling operation.
The Bangladesh Petroleum Exploration and Production Company (Bapex) began transporting heavy machinery, pipes and drilling equipment to the site yesterday morning, raising expectations that controlled drilling and technical operations could start soon.
Ukhiya Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) Panna Akter said authorities had been monitoring the situation since the fire broke out. Section 144 was imposed to ensure public safety and prevent potential hazards, including explosions and landslides. Fire Service personnel and law enforcement agencies have also been deployed.
She said a high-level expert team was assessing the gas pressure and flow, geological structure and safety requirements for extraction.
Bapex geologist Nasir Uddin said prolonged monitoring showed that gas pressure and flow remained stable. "Decisions have been taken in principle on how to control the fire safely and proceed towards commercial gas extraction," he said.
Local traders Jasim Uddin, Mohammad Ali and Mir Ahmed said heavy equipment had been arriving at the site since yesterday morning. They expressed hope that drilling operations would begin soon, potentially paving the way for Inani to become the country's 31st gas field.
Experts believe the sustained gas flow and pressure could indicate substantial underground reserves rather than a small gas pocket. However, geological surveys, seismic studies and further tests are needed to determine the size and commercial viability of the deposit.
Bangladesh has 30 discovered gas fields, around 20 of which are producing commercially. If sufficient reserves are confirmed and commercial extraction proves viable, Inani would become the country's 31st gas field, potentially strengthening energy security and reducing dependence on imports.
Gas first emerged and caught fire on October 27 during the drilling of a deep tube well at Chhoto Inani in Jaliapalong union of Ukhiya upazila. The gas was released from a depth of around 1,000 feet.

item.title: AI training free of charge with Tk 200 daily allowance: HSC pass students can apply
item.description:
The government will provide free basic training in artificial intelligence (AI) technology to young people across all 64 districts of the country to help them develop relevant skills.

The Department of Youth Development has arranged a two-month training programme for this purpose. Young people aged between 18 and 35 can apply.

The Department of Youth Development has announced that interested candidates must submit their applications by 11:59 pm on 24 November.

The training will take place under the project titled “Skills Development of IT-Literate Youth through Artificial Intelligence (AI) Technology”, implemented by the Department of Youth Development under the Ministry of Youth and Sports.

According to the relevant notice, the third batch of the “Basic Training Course on Artificial Intelligence (AI)” will run from 1 December to 31 January 2027. Participants will receive six hours of training each day, completing a total of 300 hours over 50 days.

Eligibility criteria

Applicants must have passed at least the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) or an equivalent examination. They must also have basic knowledge of computers and information technology. During the selection process, the authorities will give preference to candidates with basic computer and ICT knowledge and proficiency in English.

Interested candidates can apply through Department of Youth Development AI Project portal. The application link will close automatically after the deadline. Applicants must download and retain a copy of their application form after submission. The authorities will notify eligible applicants of the examination date, time and venue through SMS.

Important admission dates

28 November: Written examination

29 November: Viva voce

30 November: Publication of the final list of selected trainees

Applicants do not have to pay any admission fees for the training programme. In addition, non-residential trainees will receive a daily travel allowance of Tk 200.

The authorities will also provide meals every day during the training period. Participants who successfully complete the course and fulfil the prescribed requirements will receive certificates.

The authorities have divided the training programme into four regional packages.

Under Package 1, E-Learning and Earning Ltd will conduct training in 17 districts across the Dhaka and Mymensingh divisions.

Under Package 2, a joint venture comprising SEO Expert Bangladesh Ltd, European IT Solution Institute and Kaizen IT will conduct training in 16 districts across the Rajshahi and Rangpur divisions.

Under Package 3, E-Learning and Earning Ltd will conduct training in 16 districts across the Barishal and Khulna divisions.

Meanwhile, under Package 4, a joint venture comprising Service Engines Ltd, Dot Com Systems Ltd and Wizard Software Technology Bangladesh will conduct training in 15 districts across the Chattogram and Sylhet divisions.

item.title: Govt, private school admissions in 2027: Guidelines you need to know
item.description:
Students will be admitted to Class I at government and private secondary schools for the 2027 academic year through a lottery. For Classes II to IX, students will be admitted against vacant seats based on merit rankings in written examinations. To be eligible for admission to Class I, a student must be at least six years old but younger than seven. Students with special needs may receive an age relaxation of up to five years.

The Secondary and Higher Education Division of the Ministry of Education issued separate admission policies on Wednesday (11 November) and Thursday (12 November) for government and private secondary schools for the 2027 academic year. Both policies stipulate admission to Class I through a lottery and admission to subsequent classes through written examinations. They also outline the application process, distribution of marks in admission tests, fees and admission procedures.

For admission to Class I in the 2027 academic year, a student's date of birth must fall between 1 January and 31 December 2020. This means the student must have completed six years of age by 1 January 2027 but must not have turned seven. A certified copy of the online birth registration certificate must be submitted with the application as proof of age. Students with special needs may receive an additional age concession of up to five years.

The academic year at both types of schools will run from 1 January to 31 December. Each section of every class will have 55 students. Students may be admitted to the entry class of the respective school and up to Class IX, subject to seat availability.

Applications and admissions to government schools

For the 2027 academic year, applications, collection of application fees, processing and publication of results for all government secondary schools across the country will be conducted online. For admission to Class I, an applicant may select a maximum of five government schools in order of preference. If an applicant selects both shifts of a double-shift school, they will be counted as two school preferences. Multiple applications to the same school will result in the cancellation of all applications.

The Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education (DSHE) will conduct the Class I lottery centrally. Along with the list of selected students, a waiting list containing the same number of students as the available seats will also be prepared. If a selected student does not complete admission within the stipulated period, students will be admitted sequentially from the waiting list.

For Classes II to IX, written examinations will be held against vacant seats. Students will be selected according to merit rankings based on their examination results. A waiting list containing the same number of students as the vacant seats must also be prepared alongside the list of selected candidates.

Applications and admissions to private schools

The respective educational institutions will conduct admission procedures at private schools. The date and time of admission tests will be determined at meetings of the schools' management committees. To ensure that examinations at different institutions within the same catchment area are not held on the same day, schedules must be set in consultation with the relevant thana or upazila secondary education officer.

Students must be selected for Class I through a lottery. A waiting list containing the same number of students as those selected must also be maintained. For Classes II to IX, students must be admitted according to merit rankings based on written examinations against vacant seats. For admission to Class IX, candidates must be selected from among students who have passed the Class VIII or equivalent examination.

Application forms for written admission tests at private schools may be collected from the school office or, if the school has a website, from there. The dates for distribution and submission of forms must be mentioned in the admission notice.

Distribution of marks in admission tests

There are some differences in the distribution of marks for admission tests at government and private schools.

At government schools, the admission test for Classes II to V will carry a total of 50 marks. Of these, 15 will be allocated to Bangla, 15 to English and 20 to mathematics. The examination will last one hour.

For admission to Classes VI to IX, the examination will carry 100 marks, with 30 marks allocated to Bangla, 30 to English and 40 to mathematics. The examination will last two hours.

At private schools, the admission test for Classes II and III will carry a total of 50 marks, with 15 marks allocated to Bangla, 15 to English and 20 to mathematics. The examination will last one hour.

For Classes IV to IX, the examination will carry 100 marks, with 30 marks allocated to Bangla, 30 to English and 40 to mathematics. The examination will last two hours.

How much are the application and admission fees?

At government schools, the online application fee for Class I will be a maximum of Tk 110. For Classes II to IX, the fee will be a maximum of Tk 250. Admission fees, including session charges, must be determined in accordance with the Ministry of Education's instructions.

The private school admission policy also sets the maximum online application form fee at Tk 110 for Class I and Tk 250 for Classes II to IX. However, a subsequent clause in the same policy states that all MPO-listed, partially MPO-listed and non-MPO institutions, including those in Dhaka metropolitan area, may charge a maximum of Tk 200 for admission application forms. As a result, the policy contains two different amounts for application form fees.

At private schools, admission fees, including session charges, have been set according to location. The maximum fees will be Tk 500 in rural areas, Tk 1,000 in upazila municipal areas, Tk 2,000 in district headquarters municipal areas and Tk 3,000 in metropolitan areas other than Dhaka.

Non-government MPO-listed educational institutions in Dhaka metropolitan area may charge a maximum admission fee of Tk 5,000.

At partially MPO-listed institutions, the maximum amount, including monthly tuition fees, session charges and development fees, will be Tk 8,000 for Bangla-medium students and Tk 10,000 for English-version students. No institution will be allowed to collect more than Tk 3,000 under the development fee.

If a student passes the annual examination and moves to the next class at the same institution, a session charge may be collected each year, but no readmission fee may be charged. The policy also provides for fee waivers for poor, meritorious and students with special needs.

Application schedule

Neither of the two policies specifies the dates for the start and end of the admission application process.

For government schools, applications must be submitted through the designated software in accordance with the notice issued by the Dhaka City Admission Committee.

For private schools, the respective institutions will announce the dates for distribution and submission of forms and admission tests through their notices.

As a result, applicants will have to rely on the relevant admission notices for information about application opening and closing dates, examination schedules and publication of results.

item.title: Chhatra Dal: List of 13 leaders on PM’s table, when will the committee be formed
item.description:
A list of 13 leaders has been submitted to BNP Chairman and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman for the selection of the next top leadership of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal, according to multiple relevant sources.

Background checks regarding the political activities, family backgrounds and lifestyles of the potential leaders have also been conducted. There is speculation that five top leaders, including the organisation’s central president and general secretary, may be selected from this list.

This correspondent spoke to six leaders who are familiar with the process of forming the new Chhatra Dal committee and are involved in it. None could say for certain when the new committee would be announced. Their accounts had one thing in common--only the prime minister knows when the committee will be announced.

Meanwhile, new convening committees have been formed for BNP’s Dhaka north and south city units. The Dhaka north unit of Jubo Dal has also got new leadership. Efforts are underway to restructure the central committees of Jubo Dal and Swechchhasebak Dal.

However, no announcement has yet been made about the new leadership of Chhatra Dal, a key associate organisation of the BNP. As a result, those hoping to secure positions in the new committee are facing a prolonged wait.

Farewell messages, but no new committee

The current central committee of Chhatra Dal was announced on 1 March, 2024, with Rakibul Islam as president and Nasir Uddin as general secretary.

On the night of 13 August, they paid a farewell visit to BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman at his political office in Gulshan. Three other top leaders of the central committee accompanied them.

After the meeting, President Rakibul Islam posted a message on Facebook that night hinting at his departure. “The best chapter of my life is coming to an end,” he wrote. He also expressed hope that everyone would warmly welcome the upcoming new committee.

The following morning, on 14 August, General Secretary Nasir Uddin wrote on Facebook, “Today is my last day serving as the general secretary of Chhatra Dal.”

The two posts raised expectations among the organisation’s leaders and activists that a new committee would be announced soon. But no announcement followed. As a result, the leaders who had prepared to step down have had to continue carrying out organisational activities.

A top leader of the current central committee, speaking to Prothom Alo on condition of anonymity, said, “We have already said our farewells and even posted status updates on Facebook. But the new committee is not being formed. What an insulting and humiliating situation we are in! No one is even listening to us!”

Regular students or experienced leaders

Several important sources at the Prime Minister’s Office said the CVs of potential candidates for the posts of president and general secretary had been submitted to the prime minister.

According to another source, intelligence agencies had conducted detailed inquiries into 13 leaders being considered for the top positions. Reports examining their past activities, their families’ political affiliations and their current lifestyles, among other matters, had been submitted to the prime minister’s office. However, details about the identities of the 13 leaders could not be obtained.

A source familiar with the matter said there are two differing views on the criteria for selecting the new leadership.

One influential group involved in policymaking favours forming the committee with regular students. Their argument is that regular students are taking leadership positions in other student organisations, and Chhatra Dal should also give importance to this.

Another group at the policy-making level, however, favours placing relatively senior and experienced leaders in the central leadership.

The failure to reach a decision between these two positions is one of the main reasons the committee formation process has stalled. However, no one has made an official statement on the matter.

A leader whose name is being discussed for a top post told Prothom Alo on condition of anonymity, “We are completely clueless about the new committee.”

He said those who were previously involved in the committee formation process could no longer give a clear idea of when it would be announced. Everyone says the prime minister knows best.

Anxiety among aspirants

Apart from the delay in announcing the committee, the possibility that the central committees of Jubo Dal and Swechchhasebak Dal may be formed first is also worrying some Chhatra Dal leaders aspiring for top positions.

The leaders concerned said that in the past, some leaders who were left out of new Chhatra Dal committees were given responsibilities in Jubo Dal or Swechchhasebak Dal. This gave them an opportunity to remain involved in other BNP-affiliated organisations after their student politics ended.

If the committees of those two organisations are formed first this time, uncertainty may arise over where leaders who fail to secure positions in Chhatra Dal will be accommodated.

One leader aspiring for a post said maintaining communication with followers and sustaining organisational activities involved regular expenses. The prolonged wait was adding to that pressure.

Speaking on condition of anonymity, the leader also expressed concern about how he would manage his followers if he ultimately failed to secure a position in the committee.

Uncertainty affecting organisational activities

Besides carrying out organisational activities at educational institutions, Chhatra Dal plays an important role in raising students’ demands and developing the party’s future leadership.

Several Chhatra Dal leaders said a prolonged wait for central leadership could shift the focus of aspiring candidates towards securing positions in the committee, instead of maintaining regular contact with students and carrying out organisational activities.

A top leader of the current committee stressed the need for a quick decision. He said supporters of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina were trying to create instability by detonating crude bombs on different campuses.

In such a situation, he said, the uncertainty over leadership needed to be resolved so that Chhatra Dal leaders and activists could receive clear instructions and work in a coordinated manner.

Workshop tomorrow, new directives expected

Although no announcement has been made about the new committee, a daylong workshop for Chhatra Dal leaders will be held at the BNP office in Gulshan tomorrow, on Saturday, a top leader of the current central committee said.

Speaking to Prothom Alo on condition of anonymity, he said several top leaders of the central committee, presidents and general secretaries of Chhatra Dal units at all public universities and presidents and general secretaries of 10 metropolitan units were expected to attend.

They will be briefed on the promises made by the BNP before coming to power and the steps taken to implement them. They will then share the information with students at their respective campuses and units.

The leader said trainers would conduct different sessions at the workshop. Members of the cabinet are also expected to speak.

They have been informed that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman may attend in the afternoon and deliver guidance.

Several leaders involved in the Chhatra Dal committee formation process were approached for official comments. However, none agreed to make a formal statement.

item.title: Jobs counting penguins in Antarctica offer salaries of up to €2,400
item.description:
The UK-based organisation UK Antarctic Heritage Trust (UKAHT) recruits staff every year for this extraordinary job. Employees must travel to Port Lockroy in Antarctica during the southern summer.

Their duties include welcoming tourists, stamping postcards and counting penguins. Each year, the organisation selects a small team of just four or five people for the role.

The workplace is Goudier Island in the Palmer Archipelago. This small island is roughly the size of a football pitch and is covered entirely in rocks and ice. It is home to Port Lockroy, which the British established as a military base in 1944 as part of Operation Tabarin during the Second World War.

The base closed in 1962 and underwent restoration nearly 30 years later. Today, it is a protected historic site under the Antarctic Treaty System.

The site houses a small museum, a gift shop and a penguin post office. It is the southernmost operational post office in the world. Every year, thousands of tourists visit the island on cruise ships between November and March.

The selected team welcomes visitors, explains the history of the base, runs the gift shop and sorts and stamps more than 80,000 postcards each season.

The most enjoyable part of the job is counting penguins

Staff must keep a close eye on the gentoo penguins living on the island. According to UKAHT, around 1,000 penguins live there and have inhabited the island for more than 30 years.

The British Antarctic Survey (BAS), the UK's polar research institute, has carried out regular monitoring since 1996.

The main purpose is to monitor penguin breeding patterns and assess whether the presence of tourists has any adverse impact on the birds. Port Lockroy is the only place in Antarctica where researchers can study penguins throughout the entire breeding season.

Staff take great care to ensure that the penguins are not disturbed. During the first few weeks, they remain within designated boundaries. Once eggs appear in around 95 per cent of the nests, the entire team works together to count every penguin on the island.

In December 2024, they recorded 571 nests and 938 eggs. At the end of the season, they count the penguins again when the chicks have grown and begin moving around together in groups.

The counting process continues at regular intervals until two consecutive counts produce almost identical or closely matching results.

Salary and benefits: Everything you need to know

Salaries vary depending on the nature of the job. Alongside general assistant positions, there are also roles such as base manager and shop manager. Employees can earn between 1,700 euro and 2,500 euro a month, equivalent to approximately Tk 250,000 to Tk 350,000.

However, employees do not receive the entire amount as a straightforward salary. This is because those working there are classified as independent contractors or self-employed workers and receive payment based on their work.

They must therefore calculate and pay their own taxes in accordance with the relevant regulations. However, there is no need to worry about accommodation, food or protection against the extreme cold, as the organisation provides these free of charge, including the necessary warm clothing.

Living conditions on the island are challenging. There is no running water, so staff must carry drinking water in 20-litre containers from boats arriving from outside the island.

As a result, they can shower only once a week. If bad weather prevents boats from reaching the island, the team may have to go without a shower for up to two consecutive weeks.

Solar panels provide the island's only source of electricity. Consequently, staff cannot use power-hungry appliances such as hairdryers and microwave ovens.

There is also no conventional mobile phone network. For calls and communication, they must rely on limited-speed satellite internet or Wi-Fi provided by larger ships anchored nearby.

The island has a portable toilet facility, which staff must clean themselves every day. They sleep in bunk beds, while the temperature inside the barracks generally remains between 14 and 15 degrees Celsius. Outside, temperatures fluctuate between minus 5 and plus 5 degrees Celsius.

There is no upper age limit for applicants, but candidates must be at least 18 years old. A scientific academic background is not necessary either. However, applicants must be in excellent physical condition.

Daily duties include clearing snow and ice, unloading supplies from boats on slippery, rocky terrain and carrying heavy boxes weighing up to 15 kg.

Smoking is strictly prohibited on the island. Applicants must also be eligible to reside in the United Kingdom and hold valid permission to work there. Applications for these positions are expected to reopen early next year through the official website of the UK Antarctic Heritage Trust (UKAHT).

An opportunity to adopt a penguin from home

For those who cannot travel to Antarctica but love penguins and want to support them, UKAHT offers another wonderful opportunity. Anyone can adopt a gentoo penguin from the comfort of their home.

The special adoption package includes the opportunity to adopt a penguin for 12 months, a postcard sent from Antarctica, a cute penguin soft toy, an information booklet containing interesting facts, a welcome pack, an adoption certificate and regular updates about penguins at Port Lockroy.

All proceeds from this scheme go directly towards penguin care and conservation. The fund also helps cover the cost of sending a wildlife researcher to the island during the summer season.

Anyone can access all the research data on penguins through the Port Lockroy Data Portal.

item.title: Warner accuses Cricket Australia of 'cover-up' over 'Sandpapergate'
item.description:
CRICKET-SANDPAPERGATE/REVERSE SWING

David Warner blasted Cricket Australia's handling of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal as "a cover-up" on Saturday, escalating a row that has torn apart the sport.

Former opener Warner, who was banned for a year over his part in the "Sandpapergate" incident in Cape Town, lashed out at what he claimed was "a shoddy investigation".

"As far as I am aware, CA did not interview Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc or Nathan Lyon in their 2018 investigation," he said on Instagram.

"If that's correct then how can CA push the idea that the bowlers didn't know?

Australia's Khawaja claims entire team knew about 'Sandpapergate'

"It looks like they had decided who they wanted to blame from the very beginning, ran a shoddy investigation to serve the purpose and now they want to maintain the false narrative that the bowlers had no idea.

"That stinks of a cover-up."

Festering wounds over what happened in the third Test at Cape Town were re-opened this week when Usman Khawaja released his autobiography.

In the book, he alleged that the whole team knew about the plot to rough up the ball with sandpaper to make it swing.

A Cricket Australia probe concluded only then-skipper Steve Smith, his deputy Warner and Cameron Bancroft were in the know, with all three sent home from South Africa in disgrace.

Starc, Hazlewood, Lyon and Pat Cummins all denied publicly in a 2021 statement that they were aware of the plan.

On Friday, Cummins, now the Test captain, held a lengthy press conference to rubbish Khawaja's latest claims, calling them "100 percent wrong".

In response, Warner accused him of throwing close friend Khawaja "under the bus".

Starc also stated during the week that "we weren't aware of things being taken on the field". Hazlewood and Lyon have yet to comment.

Australia's Cummins says Khawaja '100pc wrong' on 'Sandpapergate'

Cricket Australia has ruled out reopening their investigation and in a statement on Saturday said all players had been given the chance to come forward.

"As we have stated previously, all players were given the opportunity to speak at the time of the initial investigation and have had the ability to come forward with new evidence in the eight years since," a spokesperson said.

"Subsequently, CA has respected every player and former players' right to provide their own version of events."

item.title: At least 26 killed in bus-truck clash in Assam
item.description:
ANI_20261113359

The death toll in the road accident in India's Assam has risen to 26, with 24 victims identified and two still unidentified, officials said on Saturday.

The accident took place on Friday, when a passenger vehicle and a container truck collided head-on in the Rongajaan area of Golaghat district, near Kaziranga National Park, police said.

Additional District Commissioner of Golaghat Jintu Bora said Jorhat Medical College had just sent another update raising the toll. "the total number of deaths has now reached 26," he told ANI.

Three teams are conducting post-mortems. One team each has arrived from Guwahati Medical College and Jorhat Medical College and 11 doctors are currently engaged in the work.

On Friday, Additional District Commissioner of Golaghat, Jintu Bora, had put the toll at 25, including 14 women and 11 men, with 23 identified. Nineteen injured people had initially been sent to Jorhat Medical College and Hospital, and two of them later died. One person at the hospital was yet to be identified.

He shared details about the identified victims, saying that nine deceased were from Nagaon district, while one was from Karbi Anglong district and another was from Bihar.

Providing details of the victim from Bihar, Bora identified him as Mohammad Rafiq Ali, son of Sami Ahmed, aged 38, whose address was listed as Tufanpur in Madhubani district.

The district administration has arranged vehicles to take the bodies to their hometowns "in a dignified manner." It is also coordinating identification and post-mortems and assisting the affected families.

Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma expressed deep grief over the accident in a post on X. "The scale of this loss has shaken all of us, and my heart goes out to every family that has lost a loved one," he wrote. "All of Assam stands with them in this hour of grief."

item.title: Police constable recruitment: Vacancies increase, competition decreases
item.description:
Bangladesh Police has received 102,694 applications for the ongoing recruitment of Trainee Recruit Constables (TRC). Although the recruitment circular was published on 9 October and applications closed on 30 October, it did not specify the number of vacancies.

However, there is now a strong possibility that 6,000 constables will eventually be recruited through this process, despite the absence of a confirmed vacancy figure in the initial announcement.

Although the number of applicants is lower than in the previous recruitment drive, the possibility of recruiting up to three times as many constables could make the competition less intense, officials concerned say.

Kamarum Munira, assistant inspector general (Media and Public Relations) at Police Headquarters, confirmed the overall recruitment figures. She told Prothom Alo that a total of 102,694 jobseekers from across the country had applied online under the ongoing recruitment circular.

Explaining the proposed recruitment numbers, Kamarum Munira said there are currently 2,000 vacant constable posts in the police force. Meanwhile, a proposal to recruit 10,000 new constables has been sent to the Ministry of Home Affairs.

Considering the approval process, the plan is to recruit 4,000 additional constables from the proposed 10,000 posts, alongside filling the existing 2,000 vacancies through the current circular. This means a total of 6,000 constables may be recruited in the ongoing process.

The remaining 6,000 posts from the proposed 10,000 will be filled in phases through subsequent recruitment circulars.

A comparison of the two recruitment drives

A comparison of the previous and current constable recruitment circulars shows several clear changes in the level of competition among applicants.

The previous recruitment circular, published in April this year, specified 2,703 constable posts. A total of 126,000 candidates applied for those positions, meaning an average of 47 applicants competed for each post.

In contrast, the current circular, published on 9 October, did not initially mention the number of vacancies. After the application process ended on October 30, a total of 102,694 applications had been received.

If the number of posts increases to 6,000 with the addition of vacancies from Police Headquarters, an average of just 17 candidates will compete for each position.

In other words, the number of applicants has fallen by around 23,000 compared with the previous recruitment drive. At the same time, the number of posts is likely to increase from 2,703 to 6,000.

As a result, candidates may have a much greater chance of securing a position in the police force than in previous recruitment drives.

Pledge of transparency at every stage

The government is emphasising the recruitment of young and skilled personnel to ensure public safety and improve the quality of services at the field level. However, regardless of the number of applicants, candidates must meet the required academic, physical and institutional qualifications to qualify for final selection.

According to the recruitment circular, candidates will have to pass several rigorous stages to be selected on merit. Their initial eligibility will first be assessed through preliminary screening. Qualified candidates will then undergo physical measurement and the Physical Endurance Test (PET), followed by a written examination and a psychological test.

Police Headquarters has issued a strict warning to ensure transparency throughout the recruitment process. No political lobbying, financial transactions or submission of false information will be tolerated beyond merit, physical fitness and eligibility.

If any false information or evidence of fraud is found at any stage of the selection process, the candidate's application will be cancelled immediately and legal action will be taken.

item.title: Garment workers protest by blocking highway in Gazipur, halting traffic
item.description:
Garment factory workers are staging a protest by blocking the Dhaka–Tangail Highway in the Chandra Palli Bidyut area of Kaliakair upazila, Gazipur. The demonstration began around 8:30 a.m. today, Saturday, bringing traffic to a standstill on both sides of the highway. The disruption has caused considerable inconvenience to commuters. In response to the situation, several nearby factories have announced temporary closures.

According to factory workers and police sources, workers from two garment factories—Tropical, located in the Chandra Palli Bidyut area of Kaliakair, and Apex Lingerie, in the Purba Chandra area—staged protests last Thursday. That day, police dispersed the workers by firing tear gas shells and sound grenades. Several workers were injured in the incident.

After reports spread that a worker injured during Thursday’s protest had died, workers stopped working and began demonstrating today. At one point, they gathered on the Dhaka–Tangail Highway near their factory in the Chandra Palli Bidyut area and blocked the road.

After receiving reports of the incident, members of the Gazipur Industrial Police, Kaliakair Police Station and Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) arrived at the scene. They are speaking with the workers and trying to restore normalcy. However, tensions escalated as the workers became agitated. The highway blockade has caused severe hardship for commuters. Many have begun walking to their destinations.

Gazipur Industrial Police Superintendent Mohammad Amzad Hossain said the workers were staging the protest based on rumours that someone had died. However, he said their main demand was an increase in wages. Workers from seven to eight nearby factories had taken to the streets.

item.title: Stench of 'Sandpapergate' set to linger as scandal reignites
item.description:
Australian captain Pat Cummins wants to draw a line under "Sandpapergate" and move on, but the stench of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal is set to linger after a week of sensational accusations and denials.
Cummins held an intense 70-minute press conference on Friday and answered every question thrown at him after former teammate Usman Khawaja reopened old wounds with the release of his explosive autobiography.
In the book, he claimed the whole team, including Cummins, knew about the plot to alter the ball with sandpaper during the Cape Town Test against South Africa.
Only David Warner, Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft were held responsible by Cricket Australia for the incident that shattered the nation's reputation, with all three sent home in disgrace and banned.
Cummins repeated multiple times that he was not aware of the plan, insisting Khawaja's version of events was "100 percent wrong".
"I don't want to talk about this again after today ... because at some point we've got to move on," he added.
His plea drew support from Justin Langer, who took over as head coach when Darren Lehmann quit in the wake of the scandal.
"Hopefully, that will put some sort of line in the sand because we have to move on," Langer told SEN radio.
"There's too many people being hurt in Australian cricket ... and that includes the Australian public.
"When I talk about Australian cricket, it's about the public, it's about the fans, it's about the players, it's about everyone who's involved: the past players, the present players, future players. We have to draw a line in the sand somewhere."
Another former Test great Greg Chappell also urged an end to the in-fighting.
"We don't want to see Australian cricket eating itself and having a little spat within the family," he told reporters.
"Hopefully Pat's put a bit of a line under it and we can start getting on with the summer of cricket."
While calls to put the issue to bed mount, it could blow up again with several key players yet to comment, notably Smith and Bancroft, while Khawaja has media commitments to sell his book.
Warner, who has strongly backed close friend Khawaja's new version of events, made clear he will not rest "until the truth is out there".
- Pick your side -
"The biggest error of the Cummins Q and A was his belief that his appearance would allow everyone to draw a line under the affair and move on," national broadcaster ABC said in an analysis.
"That's not happening. We're dealing with hurt feelings here, fractured relationships and bruised egos and nebulous concepts of truth and justice.
"You better pick your side, if you haven't already, because this is never going away."
Whether what really happened is ever properly established remains to be seen with Cricket Australia adamant it will not be re-opening its investigation.
But the bonds of a 15-year friendship between Cummins, Khawaja and Warner have splintered.
Cummins accused Khawaja of being "flippant and casual" by dropping his bombshell claims eight years after the fact, suggesting some of them were "probably defamatory".
That prompted Warner to blast Cummins for throwing Khawaja "under the bus" and The Australian newspaper to declare that "a generation of Australian players is officially at war".
Cummins insists unity within the current Australian team, which includes Smith, remains strong despite the week's firestorm as they prepare for a home Test series against New Zealand in December-January.
He said he had spoken to Smith, who lost the captaincy and was banned for a year over "Sandpapergate", and suggested the veteran batsman was keen not to regurgitate the past.
"I have spoken to Smithy. Without breaking confidence, he is done with this, he wants to move on," said Cummins.
"This was very traumatic for him. If standing up today and answering all your questions helps everyone move on, then maybe it's a good thing."

item.title: Tearful Pochettino admits Man Utd move is one of his toughest decisions
item.description:
Mauricio Pochettino said Friday that leaving his role as USA boss to take charge of Manchester United was "one of the most difficult" decisions of his career as he prepares for one of football's toughest jobs.
The 54-year-old Argentine fought back tears as he bade an emotional farewell to US football, hours after the Premier League giants announced he would replace the sacked Michael Carrick.
The former Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea boss will take up his new position on November 18, with a monumental task ahead of him.
United have made their worst start to a domestic campaign in 40 years and are languishing in the Premier League relegation zone during the current international break.
Pochettino is understood to have signed a two-and-a-half-year deal at Old Trafford, taking him through to the end of the 2028/29 season.
"We learned a lot from you all, from this amazing country," Pochettino told a media conference in Fayetteville, Georgia. "I think this was one of the most difficult decisions of (my) career."
Pochettino, who led the USA to the last 16 at this year's World Cup, will oversee back-to-back CONCACAF Nations League matches against Haiti on Saturday and next Tuesday before leaving for England.
He said he had not considered a possible return to the Premier League when he signed a contract extension with US Soccer in August, but added the opportunity to join United was too good to turn down.
"I never said I wanted to go back in the Premier League," he said. "Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives."
US Soccer CEO and secretary general JT Batson said Pochettino had left a lasting legacy through his "leadership, professionalism and commitment to our players and culture".
The federation is reportedly set to receive around $10 million in compensation, plus more to cover the departure of Pochettino's coaching staff.
United said in a statement that Pochettino was "renowned for his high-intensity, attacking style of football, his dedication to building strong, cohesive teams and his outstanding record of developing individual players".
"Pochettino has consistently performed at the highest level of football across multiple leagues," the club added.
The 20-time English champions are one of the giants of world football but have largely been also-rans since Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.
Pochettino is the eighth permanent manager tasked with returning the Red Devils to former glories.
He started his Premier League managerial career with Southampton before joining Tottenham, where he never finished lower than fifth during his five full seasons in charge and also reached the 2019 Champions League final.
Pochettino claimed the first trophies of his managerial career with PSG, collecting the 2021 French Cup and 2022 Ligue 1 title, but did not see out his contract in Paris.
He returned to the dugout at Chelsea in 2023 but only lasted one season.
The former Argentina defender, who has been linked with the United job on several previous occasions, faces a baptism of fire at the home of fierce rivals Liverpool on November 22.
He must unite a club that is deeply divided on and off the pitch.
United captain Bruno Fernandes was dropped last month after he criticised Carrick's tactics and Lisandro Martinez took a public swipe at the United hierarchy over a lack of investment.
Angry fans vented their frustration at the club's ownership following the sacking of the popular Carrick, who won multiple trophies as a player.
Despite fierce and persistent protests over two decades, the US-based Glazer family still hold a majority stake in United, which Malcolm Glazer bought via a leveraged takeover in 2005, saddling the club with huge debts.
Any hopes the arrival of British billionaire Jim Ratcliffe as a minority owner in 2024 would signal a new dawn have since faded.
Carrick issued an emotional statement Friday wishing United "nothing but success", adding that his love for the club "never dies".

item.title: Bangladesh face Pakistan in crucial SAFF semifinal today
item.description:
Bangladesh will look to move one step closer to ending their 23 years wait for a second SAFF Championship title when they lock-horn Pakistan in a crucial semifinal at the National Stadium here on Saturday.
The match kicks off at 8:30 pm and will be televised live by private satellite channel T Sports. Defending champions India will face Bhutan in the first semifinal at 3 pm on the same day.
The hosts headed into the knockout clash full of confidence after topping Group A with a perfect record, winning both their matches without conceding a goal.
The hosts promised an exciting contest as they look to turn their impressive group-stage performance into a place in the title-deciding match.
The boys in red and green started their tournament campaign with a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Bhutan before earning an overwhelming 4-0 victory over Sri Lanka in their final group match.
Thanks to Shamit Shome, Hamza Choudhury, Farhaan Ali Wahid and Rakib Hossain who were on target against Sri Lanka, demonstrating Bangladesh's attacking strength and growing confidence.
Earlier, Bangladesh midfielder Jamal Bhuyan already acknowledged the threat posed by Pakistan, saying the team has shifted their focus to the semifinal following their convincing win over Sri Lanka.
The hosts, however, have some injury concerns in their defensive department. Right-back Saad Uddin has been ruled out of the remainder of the tournament after sustaining an Achilles tendon injury against Sri Lanka.
The availability and fitness of other defenders will also be important for the coaching staff ahead of the crucial encounter.
Bangladesh will also get the home ground advantage as they will get bounty support from their passionate football fans.
Hamza and Co. seek to reach the final in front of their supporters.
A victory would take Bangladesh one step closer to ending their long wait for regional football glory.
The challenges are particularly high for Bangladesh, who are chasing their second SAFF Championship title after lifting the trophy for the first back in 2003 in home ground. The boys in red and green have been waiting for 23 years to reclaim the regional crown.
With a place in the final at stake, Bangladesh will need to maintain their attacking momentum against a determined Pakistan side.
However, Pakistan are also expected to provide a much tougher challenge in the semifinal against Bangladesh.
Pakistan began their campaign with a fighting 3-2 goals defeat to India in their opening group match before bounced back to register a convincing 3-0 goals win over Maldives in their final group match.

item.title: Silva says Portugal ready for spotlight without Ronaldo
item.description:
Portugal midfielder Bernardo Silva said Friday his team could cope with any extra pressure on them following Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement, ahead of their first match without the superstar forward.
Jorge Jesus's side host Denmark in Braga on Saturday in the Nations League, with a tribute planned for their all-time leading goalscorer.
Real Madrid's Silva, who inherits the captain's armband from Ronaldo, admitted that the striker had been the main focus for much of the past two decades but backed the team to cope with the pressure in the 41-year-old's absence.
"Everyone knows the weight Cristiano carries. Most people went to the stadium to see Cristiano, many went just for him, and that's not going to happen now," Silva told reporters.
"The national team players are used to the spotlight, the pressure, and the responsibility, as well as being pointed at when things don't go well -- so that's not an issue."
Portugal will pay tribute to five-time Ballon d'Or winner Ronaldo before the game against Denmark, with media reporting the squad will walk out wearing number seven jerseys, Ronaldo's number.
Whether Ronaldo will be present is unknown, after he fell out with veteran coach Jorge Jesus in September.
Last week Ronaldo said he was bringing down the curtain on his storied international career.
Ronaldo made his debut for Portugal in 2003 and went on to play a world record 234 times for his country, scoring 146 goals.
"Nobody can forget Cris's 23 years in the national team and everything he did," Jesus told reporters.
"I think (paying tribute) is a brilliant idea to continue to remind us that he is a legend of Portuguese football."
Portugal have already sealed qualification to the quarter-finals of the Nations League, winning all four matches in Group A4.

item.title: Argentina beaten by Uruguay in first game since Messi retirement
item.description:
Argentina suffered a 2-1 defeat against Uruguay on Friday in their first game since Lionel Messi's retirement from international football.
A second-half own goal by Argentina defender Leonardo Balerdi followed by a fluky effort from Uruguay midfielder Maxi Araujo sealed defeat for the 2026 World Cup runners-up.
Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alavarez gave Argentina hope of a comeback with a 73rd-minute strike but Uruguay held on to clinch a third victory for new manager Diego Forlan.
Messi played his final game for Argentina in an emotional farewell friendly victory over Benin last month, calling time on a glittering career that spanned 207 caps and 125 goals.
With the 39-year-old genius missing, Argentina struggled to break down a resilient Uruguay team for long stretches of Friday's friendly.
Nico Paz had Argentina's best chance of the first half, but saw his shot well-saved by Uruguay goalkeeper Cristopher Fiermarin.
Uruguay made the breakthrough soon after half-time when a Giorgian de Arrascaeta free-kick from the left caused chaos in the Argentina defence.
Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez attempted to clear with a header but his effort instead cannoned off team-mate Balerdi and into the net.
De Arrascaeta then set up Uruguay's second in the 53rd minute, his corner appearing to hit Araujo's shoulder before looping high into the net.
Alvarez pulled a goal back midway through the half, and had another good chance in stoppage time but Uruguay closed out the win.

item.title: The miracle cure in your Facebook feed is killing Bangladeshis
item.description:
Every Bangladeshi family knows the scene. My father is newly diagnosed with diabetes. The doctor's advice is the same as always: Medication, diet, regular monitoring, lifelong discipline. It is sound advice, and it is exhausting to follow.
Then his morning walk friend forwards a video to him. A man in a white coat promises a cure in seven days, with no injections and no side effects, for only Tk3,500 and cash on delivery.
This is not harmless chatter. It is a business, and its customers are dying.
Diabetes is a lifelong condition for which no cure currently exists. That inconvenient truth is the foundation of a thriving commercial ecosystem on Facebook and TikTok: Fake doctors, unregistered supplements, and "miracle" pills sold to people who are frightened, tired, or simply priced out of regular care.
Social media is filled with products claiming to replace insulin or conventional medication with herbal alternatives, despite no credible scientific evidence supporting those claims. Patients each month require hospitalization after following unqualified health advice found on social media and resulting in liver, kidney, or cardiovascular complications.
Think about what that number means. Families continue to pay for someone else's marketing copy with their organs. Now think about the patients who never made it to a hospital.
The word "herbal" does a great deal of the sellers' work. In a country with a long and respected tradition of traditional remedies, "natural" feels "safe." It is not.
A product with no declared dose, no tested purity, and no registration is simply an unknown substance. The danger is greatest when a patient stops a prescribed drug because a post told them they no longer need it.
What makes this scam distinctly Bangladeshi is how skilfully it borrows trust. Fraudsters know we respect the doctor, the professor, and the familiar newspaper masthead, so they counterfeit all three.
Dr Jahangir Kabir, a prominent health advocate who promotes lifestyle-based approaches to diabetes, has said dishonest groups are misusing his name to sell unregulated medicines.
He reports that hundreds of fake Facebook pages were created in his name, some even mimicking his verified profile's blue-badge image. A man who tells people to change how they eat and live found his face on the label of a bottle.
He is not alone. Microbiologist Dr Senjuti Saha discovered that her name and image were being used in a fraudulent campaign and filed a general diary at the police station.
Dismislab traced the "Optimax" diabetes product to counterfeit pages mimicking Prothom Alo, featuring fake interviews with "prominent" Bangladeshi professionals.
Even the health minister's identity has been hijacked: iIn 2024 the ministry had to warn that fake Facebook accounts were being opened in his name, with advertisements that could cheat the public.
When the scammer can wear the face of a trusted doctor and the logo of a trusted newspaper, "just don't believe everything online" is not advice. It is an abdication.
We have long assumed that more smartphones meant more awareness. The evidence is more troubling. Studies suggest that mobile phone ownership is associated with greater exposure to misinformation, not just greater access to information.
In a country where phones have reached the village before the specialist has, the same device that delivers a telemedicine consultation also delivers a "cure" for diabetes. In many cases, it is the second that arrives first.
Self-medication was already common long before Facebook. We buy tablets over the counter, trust a neighbour's prescription, and stretch a doctor's visit as far as it will go. Influencers did not create this habit. They have simply learned to monetize it.
Media professionals are not blameless. For years our response to health misinformation has been the occasional "myth-buster" column, published once, read by few, and forgotten by the next news cycle. The scammers publish daily. We cannot answer a daily campaign with an annual correction.
Newspapers need standing health fact-check desks, with trained reporters, a medical advisory panel, and the same institutional seriousness we give to political fact-checking. A fake diabetes ad should be treated with the same urgency as a fake political quote.
Television channels and online portals should produce short, shareable "spot the scam" segments in Bangla. Sixty seconds are enough to show a viewer how to check whether a doctor is registered with the Bangladesh Medical and Dental Council, why "cure in seven days" is a warning rather than a promise, and why no pill replaces insulin. Content that is easy to forward to the family WhatsApp group is how we compete on the scammers' own ground.
We should use AI sensibly. Newsrooms can deploy language tools, including Bangla-capable ones, to flag viral health claims, repeated ad creatives, and suspicious pages at a scale no human desk can match.
But AI should only flag. Verification, context, and the final call must remain with trained editors and doctors. A machine can tell us where the fire is. It cannot tell us whether the person in the video is really a physician.
Finally, the media must stop accepting the framing that this is merely a "content moderation" problem. Content moderation means a platform deciding whether a post stays up.
What we are describing is the sale of unregistered medicinal products, under false identities, to sick people, for profit. That is consumer fraud and a public health offense.
The Directorate General of Drug Administration, the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission, the consumer rights authorities and law enforcement all have a role.
So do Meta and TikTok, which earn revenue from the very advertisements that deceive our citizens.
The press should keep asking the uncomfortable questions: Who approved this ad, who was paid, who was prosecuted, and how many times was it reported before it came down?
The next time a "miracle cure" appears in your feed, remember what it is: Someone's sales pitch, aimed at your parent's fear.
Insulin is not a conspiracy, and diabetes does not end in seven days. The sooner we say so, loudly, every single day, the fewer families will learn it in a hospital corridor.
Dewan Shahnoor Alam Sourav is a lecturer in the Department of Media Studies and Journalism at the University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh (ULAB). Can be reached at ds.alam.sourav@gmail.com .

item.title: How do I grieve someone I have not met yet?
item.description:
This is what I kept asking myself as I waited in the hospital, knowing that my 4.5-month pregnancy was coming to an end. Perhaps it is simply human nature to grow attached to the life growing inside you.
My entire life, I have catastrophized everything. The same happened when I found out I was pregnant. But I quickly tried to quiet that part of me and focus on doing my best.
Everything was going perfectly. I had no known risk factors, my scans had gone well, and my doctor had told me to schedule an appointment for the following month.
No one had warned me that even when everything seemed to be going well, it could all turn upside down in the blink of an eye.
I had gone to sleep when my amniotic fluid ruptured. Even half asleep, I knew what that meant. My pregnancy had ended. I was rushed to the hospital, and the duty doctor tried to console me: “We do not know yet.”
But I knew that the future I had already started imagining would no longer come to be.
I had to wait an excruciating 12 hours for my gynaecologist to examine me. She finally explained what would happen next. I would be given one dose of medication that day and more the following day to induce labour.
Miscarriage . Just one word, carrying a weight that is almost impossible to put into words. A grief so profound, yet one no one warns you about.
While I waited in the hospital for the procedures to be completed, my aunts, uncles, grandmothers, cousins, everyone, rallied around me. I was going through one of the most difficult periods of my life, but I was wrapped in a blanket of love.
The women around me told me their own stories of loss, their struggles, and how they had found a way through. Even though my own pain felt insurmountable, it was the strength I found in their stories that helped me through.
Despite medical science coming such a long way, no reason could be identified for why this was happening to me. The pregnancy was not advanced enough for there to be any hope of saving it, but it was also not early enough for my miscarriage to go unnoticed.
The medication I was given sent my body into what felt like a state of shock. I was shivering uncontrollably, and when the shivering stopped, my body would have to endure contractions. I had to feel the pain of labour, but there was no baby to hold at the end of it.
Nothing could be done to ease my pain, knowing that there was no possibility of a different ending. I was handed a death certificate for someone who never even had a birth certificate.
It is estimated that one in four to six pregnancies ends in miscarriage. But the statistics are complex. There are a multitude of factors that can play a role.
Most of the websites I have visited state that miscarriages are common. And this makes me question: Why is there so little conversation about something that affects women so deeply?
A pregnancy loss is deeply personal, and it should always be a woman’s prerogative to decide whether she wants to talk about it. But for those who do want to talk about it, do we have enough safe spaces?
There is so little mental health support for women going through a loss like this. I was genuinely grateful for the hospital staff who consoled me, who held my hand when my body was going through unbearable pain, and for the doctors who treated me with respect and dignity. But is that guaranteed for every woman who experiences a loss like this?
Too often, these losses are minimised with statements such as, “It was not meant to be.” As though a few words can make the grief disappear. We should hold space for women who are going through these losses and create more meaningful systems of support.
When even “rich” countries struggle to fund research into miscarriage and pregnancy loss, there is little hope for a country like Bangladesh.
The world can be an extremely cruel place for women. But I refuse to be anything but kind to myself.
There was a version of me that existed before the miscarriage, and there is a version of me that exists now. I do not think they are the same person.
The trivial things in life that used to bother me no longer seem to matter. Things I once thought were important have suddenly lost weight. There is something about losing something so deeply wanted that changes your understanding of what truly matters.
While I do not want my pregnancy loss to define me, I also cannot pretend that it is not a part of who I am now. I will carry this loss with me, and I will not allow it to be swept under the carpet or reduced to something that simply happened and should be forgotten.
I am still grieving the future I do not get to have. There is no linear path through a loss this profound. I was applauded for being brave, but the truth is, I was forced to be brave.
I no longer want to be courageous. I want to mourn. I want to grieve the life I never got to meet, on my own terms.
It is the strength of my parents, partner, and siblings that has kept me going. Life keeps moving forward, even though it felt like mine had stopped for a while.
The only lesson I carry forward is that I will show up with love, strength, and support for any woman who has gone through something similar. There should be more conversations about this reality, about a kind of loss that can be so profound and yet have no logical answers. Women should be allowed to grieve without being told how they should grieve.
Ahona Hassan is a human rights activist passionate about speaking on issues often left unspoken.

The second half is already 10 minutes old, but neither side has found the net. Rakib took a very good shot, but it was blocked by a Pakistan defender. Moments later, Shamit Shome was almost in a good position to receive Suki’s cutback inside the box, but Abdullah got to the ball first and cleared it.

First half ended goalless 

The referee has blown the whistle to signal the end of the first half. Neither side has managed to score. Both teams have produced some promising attacks, but neither has found the net. Bangladesh and Pakistan have both hit the woodwork. Bangladesh’s attacks have repeatedly come to a halt just outside Pakistan’s penalty area.

Bangladesh ahead in ball possession 

Bangladesh have maintained 65 per cent of ball posession after 40 minutes.

Pakistan hit the post

The referee called a cooling break in the 30th minute. Pakistan have looked dangerous going forward since then. Tariq Kazi failed to mark his man properly, allowing Abdus Samad to get a shot away in space. But his effort struck the post.

Rakib nearly scored for Bangladesh!

Bangladesh came agonisingly close to scoring!

Rakib unleashed a powerful shot after receiving a header from Shamit Shome. Pakistan’s goalkeeper initially saved the effort, but the ball then struck the post. Bangladesh were left frustrated as the goal narrowly eluded them.

After 20 minutes

Another 10 minutes have passed, with both teams competing on equal terms. The flurry of attacks seen in the opening 10 minutes has since subsided.

Bangladesh have moved forward with the ball on several occasions but have struggled to make progress near the penalty area. They are finding it difficult to cope with the physical strength of Pakistan’s defenders.

10 minutes

The first 10 minutes have passed. Pakistan put Bangladesh under some early pressure, but Bangladesh are gradually settling into the game and have started making attacking moves of their own.

Kazem Shah had a shot on target in the seventh minute, but it lacked power and caused little trouble for the Pakistan goalkeeper.

Two attacks in two minutes

Pakistan launched two promising attacks in the opening two minutes. One move, which began with a misplaced pass by Shamit Shome, resulted in a shot on target, but Mehedi Hasan Srabon produced an excellent save.

The attack in the following minute did not reach the goalkeeper. Pakistan have made a confident start, putting Bangladesh under some early pressure.

Kick-off!

The referee blows the whistle, and the Bangladesh–Pakistan semi-final is underway at the National Stadium in Dhaka. Both teams are now chasing a place in the SAFF Championship final. Can Bangladesh end their 21-year wait for a place in the title decider?

Head to Head: Bangladesh ahead

Bangladesh hold the edge in the head-to-head record between the two sides. Of their 17 meetings, Bangladesh have won seven, while Pakistan have won six. The remaining four matches ended in draws.

VAR in place

A quick reminder: this match will have VAR (Video Assistant Referee). The technology made its debut at Dhaka’s National Stadium this afternoon during the first semi-final between India and Bhutan. It will also be in use for Bangladesh’s match.

So, players and fans will need to be a little cautious before celebrating. The referee’s decision could be overturned following a VAR review.

India await

The Bangladesh–Pakistan match is the second semi-final of the tournament. India have already secured their place in the final, beating Bhutan 2–1 in the first semi-final.

Read the story here: Bhutan’s fate unchanged after 18 years as India reach final

Two changes in Bangladesh starting XI

Bangladesh have made two changes to their starting XI from the match against Sri Lanka. One was unavoidable, as Saad Uddin has been ruled out of the tournament with an injury. Rahmat Mia replaces him in the starting XI today.

The other change is at centre-forward, where Shuki Itofusa replaces Mohammad Ibrahim.

Bangladesh XI: Mehedi Hasan Srabon, Zidan Yusuf, Tariq Kazi, Zayan Ahmed, Rahmat Mia, Hamza Choudhury, Shamit Shome, Kazem Shah, Farhan Ali, Rakib Hossain and Shuki Itofusa.

After 21 years!

Today’s match is about more than just a place in the final. It offers Bangladesh an opportunity to end a 21-year wait. The last time Bangladesh played in the SAFF Championship final was in 2005.

On 14 December that year, Bangladesh secured their place in the final by beating Pakistan in the semi-final at Karachi’s People’s Stadium. In the more than two decades since then, Bangladesh have been eliminated at different stages, sometimes in the group phase and sometimes in the semi-finals. Despite coming close to the final, they have failed to reach it again.

Read more in this report: Bangladesh face Pakistan again with final in sight, 21 years after Karachi triumph

Welcome

Bangladesh face Pakistan in a battle for a place in the SAFF Championship final. Follow our live blog for all the latest developments from the match at the National Stadium in Dhaka.
