item.title: Case filed against MP Nusrat’s father over alleged land grabbing, vandalism
item.description:
A case has been filed against Abdul Halim, father of reserved women’s seat MP and National Citizen Party (NCP) leader Nusrat Tabassum, over allegations of demolishing a house, assault, looting and grabbing land in Daulatpur Upazila of Kushtia.
Idris Ali, 67, of Bagoan village in Mathurapur Union, filed the case with Daulatpur Police Station on Saturday. Halim is the sole named accused, while eight to 10 unidentified people have also been accused.
Kushtia Additional Superintendent of Police Faisal Mahmud confirmed the case, saying Sub-Inspector Mohsin Chowdhury would investigate it.
According to the complaint, Ali bought 4.25 kathas of land from Halim’s two brothers around five years ago, took possession and built a house there. He alleged that Halim later planned to take over the property.
The complaint said Halim and his associates attacked Ali’s house with locally made weapons on September 13 last year, damaging its fencing, doors, windows, tin roof and furniture, causing losses estimated at Tk250,000.
Ali and his wife, Mina Khatun, were allegedly beaten when they tried to resist. The attackers also allegedly took away three beds, 10 bundles of tin sheets and other valuables worth around Tk150,000.
Ali further alleged that Halim filed a separate case against him on September 16 last year, leading to his imprisonment. After securing bail, he learnt that Halim had occupied the disputed land, allegedly using his daughter’s influence.
Ali said threats of being implicated in an arms case forced him and his family to leave the area and take shelter at his in-laws’ home.
He said he had delayed filing the case because of threats and security concerns. He also expressed fear that he and his family could be falsely implicated in a case over a fire at Halim’s house on November 12.
Contacted over the allegations, Halim said he was unaware of the case. He claimed Ali had disputes with several people in the area and had been in hiding since August 5, 2024. He suggested Ali might have filed the case at someone else’s instigation.
The case comes days after a fire broke out at Nusrat’s ancestral home early on November 12. Nusrat and other NCP leaders alleged that petrol bombs had been used in the attack.
Speaking in parliament on Thursday, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said investigators initially believed no petrol bombs had been used and that an electrical short circuit was a likely cause because of old wiring. He said action would be taken if further investigation established sabotage.
However, on Friday, Tozammel Haque, an assistant general manager of the Pragpur Rural Electricity Sub-Zone Office in Kushtia, said an inspection of the meter, wiring and main switch found no signs of a short circuit. He also said the cut-out and transformer fuse were intact.

item.title: Norwegian journalist who questioned Modi denied entry to India
item.description:
A Norwegian journalist who publicly questioned Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his reluctance to face the press has been barred from travelling to India, triggering fresh concerns about press freedom and the treatment of foreign journalists critical of the government.
Helle Lyng Svendsen, a journalist with Norway’s Dagsavisen newspaper, said her Indian visa was cancelled on November 11, just minutes before she was scheduled to leave for the airport to attend the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad.
She had been invited to speak about the future of media and press freedom at the November 13–14 conference, organized by the Congress-led Telangana government.
According to Svendsen, the Indian Embassy in Oslo contacted her approximately 10 minutes before her departure and informed her that she could not travel, despite having received a visa and political clearance.
In a video message addressed to Indian Home Minister Amit Shah, she alleged that the cancellation followed instructions from India’s Ministry of Home Affairs.
Svendsen questioned whether the decision was linked to her criticism of Modi and his government, describing it as potentially politically motivated.
The journalist attracted international attention during Modi’s visit to Oslo on May 18, when she challenged him for leaving a joint media appearance with Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre without taking journalists’ questions.
Modi did not respond.
Svendsen subsequently raised questions about human rights and press freedom during another briefing with Indian officials, leading to a tense exchange.
She has also published criticism of Modi’s government and prominent Indian business figures.
The visa cancellation prompted the Association of Norwegian Editors and the Norwegian Press Association to write to the Indian Embassy in Oslo on November 13, seeking an explanation.
The organizations warned that refusing entry to journalists because of their reporting or questions would undermine press freedom.
They also sought assurances that Norwegian journalists would not face similar restrictions.
The controversy comes amid longstanding criticism of India’s treatment of foreign journalists and restrictions on independent reporting.
The dispute has also widened politically.
Congress MP Shashi Tharoor alleged on Friday that 115 of 315 speakers cleared for the summit were denied entry or had their visas cancelled.
India’s Ministry of External Affairs responded that visa decisions were a sovereign matter, without publicly explaining Svendsen’s case.
The Home Ministry had not issued a public response at the time of reporting.

item.title: RMG owners warn to quit wage talks over factory security
item.description:
Garment factory owners have warned that they will not participate in ongoing Minimum Wage Board discussions unless comprehensive security is ensured for industrial units, noting that 147 factories across major industrial belts remain non-operational due to persistent unrest.
The warning came at a joint press conference held by the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) and the Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA) at BGMEA Building in Uttara on Saturday.
BGMEA President Mahmud Hasan Khan and BKMEA Executive President Fazlee Shamim Ehsan spoke in the press conference.
Leaders of the two apex trade bodies stated that a vested group is attempting to create anarchy under the guise of minimum wage demands, keeping numerous factories closed for seven to 12 days across Savar, Ashulia, Narayanganj, and Gazipur.
According to the trade bodies, while the vast majority of workers are eager to return to work, a small faction—joined by outsiders—is creating disturbances, obstructing willing workers, and pelting stones at operational factories.
Currently, 147 member factories employing roughly 300,000 workers are completely unable to operate. Of these, 55 factories have been closed, while 92 others failed to resume production despite attempts to operate. Owners noted that although Section 13(1) of the Labor Act prevents arbitrary closures, the prevailing unsafe environment has left them with no choice.
PBGMEA and BKMEA members unanimously termed it "illogical" to vandalize factories while simultaneously negotiating wage hikes. They urged the government to deploy maximum law enforcement personnel to restore order and protect industrial assets.
The owners announced that they will observe the situation until Sunday. If normalcy returns by then, they will submit their formal wage proposal at the Minimum Wage Board meeting scheduled for Monday. Otherwise, the associations warned they will be forced to take tough organizational decisions.
Leaders of BGMEA and BKMEA and different factory owners were present at the press conference.
Earlier, the business leaders organised a consulting meeting among them regarding the present situation of law and order and labor unrest in the apparel sector in Bangladesh.

item.title: Tk7cr Shanti Nibash remains unused in Gopalganj
item.description:
A 25-bed Shanti Nibash (Old Home), built in Tungipara of Gopalganj to provide shelter and care for destitute, helpless, and abandoned elderly women, remains non-operational due to a shortage of manpower and lack of maintenance.
The Tk6.96 crore facility was constructed under a government project titled “Establishment of 25-bed Shanti Nibash in Eight Government Children's Homes”, implemented by the Department of Social Services under the Ministry of Social Welfare.
Although construction was completed several years ago, the building and its furniture are gradually deteriorating due to a lack of maintenance.
The project began on July 1, 2020, with an initial completion deadline of June 2022. However, work was disrupted by the Covid-19 pandemic, prompting an extension until June 2023 under the first revised project plan.
The project's initial estimated cost was Tk73.98 crore, which was later increased to Tk82.69 crore in the revised Development Project Proposal (DPP) following an expansion in the scope of work.
Messrs Kohinoor Enterprise completed the construction of the facility at a cost of Tk6 crore 96 lakh 45 thousand. The Department of Social Services implemented the project under the Ministry of Social Welfare.
According to the ministry, the Tungipara facility is exclusively designated for elderly women and has accommodation for 25 residents. Plans include residential facilities, healthcare, recreation, physical exercise, prayer spaces and training opportunities.
On November 14, 2023, then prime minister Sheikh Hasina inaugurated the 25-bed Shanti Nibash and a child daycare centre at the government children's home in Gopalganj, along with several other projects, through a video conference from Ganabhaban.
The ministry also planned to establish similar Shanti Nibash facilities in other districts, replacing conventional old-age homes, to ensure a dignified and secure life for vulnerable elderly people.
During a visit to the facility inside the Tungipara Destitute Children's Training and Rehabilitation Centre around 11 am on Tuesday, this correspondent found the three-storey building standing to the east of the centre's academic and administrative buildings.
An inauguration plaque bearing the date November 14 and the name of then prime minister Sheikh Hasina is installed at the front of the building.
The ground floor houses a doctor's room, a gym, a dining room, a kitchen and a substation. The second floor has a study room and five bedrooms, each containing three beds.
The third floor has six rooms, including a management room, a study room, and four bedrooms.
Each bedroom has three beds with mattresses, three wardrobes, chairs and tables, as well as an attached bathroom.
However, the mattresses were found covered in dust and dirt during the visit. The middle sections of the floors were also damp, indicating a prolonged lack of cleaning and maintenance. The condition raises concerns about the building's upkeep and readiness to accommodate residents.
Shila Saha, supervisor (assistant director) of the Destitute Children's Training and Rehabilitation Centre, said construction of the Shanti Nibash had been completed long ago, but the facility could not be opened due to a shortage of required manpower.
“We occasionally clean the ground floor of the building. However, the second and third floors are not cleaned regularly,” she said.
She added that the construction was not handled locally, as the ministry directly oversaw the entire process, including tendering and implementation.

item.title: Rizvi: Hasina has no legal scope to obtain passport
item.description:
BNP Acting Secretary General and Prime Minister’s Political Adviser Advocate Ruhul Kabir Rizvi on Saturday said fugitive Awami League leader Sheikh Hasina has no legal scope to obtain a passport.
He said Hasina must serve all the punishments handed down to her for crimes against humanity, killings of people, students and workers, while she must also face the ongoing trials against her.
Rizvi made the remarks after a protest procession organised by Dhaka Metropolitan South Jubo Dal against the alleged terrorism and anarchy of the activities-banned Awami League.
The procession started from the National Press Club and ended at Shahbagh intersection.
Rizvi said Sheikh Hasina's father, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman had also established fascist rule through the formation of BAKSAL.
Referring to the law of 1973, he described Sheikh Hasina as a fugitive accused of crimes against humanity, saying she could not return to the country and must serve the punishment imposed on her under the law.
Addressing Jubo Dal and BNP leaders and activists, Rizvi said cocktail explosions and arson attacks could not intimidate leaders and activists of Jatiyatabadi Jubo Dal and other associate organisations of the BNP.
He said they had continued their struggle with courage despite enforced disappearances, killings and various forms of repression. Jubo Dal Dhaka Metropolitan South Member Secretary Rabiul Islam Nayan had also faced severe torture and physical abuse, but such repression had failed to make them bow their heads.
Rizvi further said nationalist forces could not be subdued, adding that nationalist and democratic forces across the country would build resistance on the streets against any attempt to revive fascism.
Rabiul Islam Nayan and other leaders and activists of Dhaka Metropolitan South Jubo Dal were present at the programme.

item.title: Bobby Deol wraps up Aashram season 4 shoot
item.description:
Bobby Deol and filmmaker Prakash Jha have wrapped filming for the 4th season of their crime drama series Aashram, marking the latest milestone in the popular franchise.
The cast and crew celebrated the completion of the shoot with a cake-cutting ceremony. The cake carried the message, “Japnaam, It’s a Wrap – Aashram Season 4”, as Deol and Jha joined the celebrations.
Deol will reprise his role as Baba Nirala, the self-proclaimed godman whose mysterious and power-hungry persona has remained at the centre of the series since its debut in August 2020.
Conceptualized and directed by Jha, Aashram explores blind faith, power, manipulation and exploitation. The filmmaker’s collaboration with Deol has been central to the show's identity across its previous instalments.
The franchise has released 3 seasons so far, with the third season split into 2 parts. The upcoming instalment is expected to continue Baba Nirala’s story and explore the shifting relationships among the characters surrounding him.
While filming has wrapped, the makers have yet to announce a release date for the new season.

item.title: 118 Dhaka waterbodies set for restoration
item.description:
Decades of unplanned urbanisation, illegal occupation and landfilling have pushed many of Dhaka's canals, ponds and natural waterbodies to the brink of disappearance. Now, the government has launched an initiative to reclaim and restore 118 of them through the two city corporations.
The plan covers 56 canals and 62 ponds, with the aim of improving drainage, protecting the environment and restoring the capital's natural water flow.
According to recent data from the National River Conservation Commission and Dhaka district administration, the capital has 56 canals — 29 under Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) and 27 under Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC). Many have been encroached upon, restricting or blocking their natural flow.
DSCC administrator Md Abdus Salam said the corporation plans to reclaim the canals, demarcate their boundaries and construct retaining walls along both banks.
A project is already under way to reclaim the Shyampur, Manda, Jirani and Kalunagar canals, while other canals under the southern city corporation will be addressed in phases.
In DNCC areas, work to reclaim 10 canals has begun as an initial step. These include Kallyanpur, Rupnagar, Baunia, Diabari, Abdullahpur, Ibrahimpur, Baishteki, Katasur, Ramchandrapur and Begunbari.
Encroachment has led to houses, apartment buildings, shops, markets, workshops, garages, factories and warehouses being built on canal land. Such structures have narrowed or blocked waterways, worsening waterlogging across the city.
Urban experts say the loss of natural water channels has disrupted drainage, damaged biodiversity and increased pressure on groundwater resources. Even moderate rainfall can now cause waterlogging in many parts of Dhaka.
Dhaka University's Department of Criminology Assistant Professor and Chairman Md Rezaul Karim Sohag said the disappearance of canals had obstructed the flow of water and waste towards rivers, contributing to the city's drainage problems.
He warned that preventing fresh encroachment after reclamation would be the biggest challenge, noting that previous eviction drives had often failed to prevent illegal structures from returning due to inadequate monitoring and maintenance.
The DNCC said several agencies would be involved in the process, including the district administration, Water Development Board and Dhaka Metropolitan Police. Their responsibilities include verifying land records, identifying government property, demarcating canal boundaries and carrying out lawful eviction drives.
The Department of Environment's Deputy Director Sabrin Sultana said legal action would be taken against those who dump waste into canals and cause pollution or environmental damage.
Experts say restoring the waterways and ponds could help rainwater drain more quickly, support groundwater recharge and protect habitats for aquatic life and birds. Preserved waterbodies could also serve as emergency water sources and help reduce urban heat.
They also say planned greenery and walkways along restored canals could improve the city's public spaces and environmental conditions.

item.title: Dengue claims 8 more lives, 1,674 hospitalized
item.description:
Eight more people have died from dengue, while 1,674 others were hospitalized with the mosquito-borne disease across the country in the 24 hours up to 8am on Saturday.
The total number of dengue-related deaths this year has reached 491.
The information was disclosed in a press release issued by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) on Saturday.
According to the press release, among the newly hospitalized patients, 714 were from Dhaka division, 50 from Mymensingh division, 311 from Chittagong division, 190 from Khulna division, 115 from Rajshahi division, 60 from Rangpur division, 213 from Barisal division and 21 from Sylhet division.
Since the beginning of this year, a total of 160,557 dengue patients have been admitted to hospitals across the country, according to the DGHS.
Of them, 154,151 patients have been discharged from hospitals, while 5,915 are currently receiving treatment.

item.title: DU restricts entry of outside vehicles to campus
item.description:
Dhaka University (DU) authorities have decided to restrict the entry and movement of outside vehicles on campus, citing security concerns and the need to ensure the safety of students and the university community.
The decision was announced in an urgent notice issued by the Office of the Proctor on Saturday.
Under the notice, vehicles belonging to people other than university teachers, students, officers and employees will face restrictions.
However, vehicles bearing Dhaka University stickers, ambulances, those carrying doctors and patients, journalists' vehicles, ride-sharing services, food delivery vehicles, online shopping deliveries and other government vehicles will be allowed to enter the campus.
The notice also said university authorities reserve the right to search any person or vehicle for security reasons.

item.title: NBR reaches out to retailers to cover revenue shortfall
item.description:
To collect an advance tax of Tk2 per thousand on goods supplied to retailers, the National Board of Revenue (NBR) is moving to leverage information technology.
The agency has initiated the development of a specialized app for this purpose. The NBR’s IT wing has already begun work on the software, which is expected to be finalized for use starting next January, sources within the NBR revealed.
The budget for the current FY27 imposes a 0.2% advance tax on the supply of goods to retail vendors.
This means Tk2 will be deducted in advance for every Tk1,000 worth of supplied goods.
Although this provision has previously been kept in budgets, the NBR is now taking active steps to implement it.
Initially, this tax will be collected through the distributors of large manufacturing firms. Distributors will be required to use a dedicated app.
The app will maintain records of sales to retailers, issue receipts, and automatically generate e-invoices.
It will also feature options for receiving product payments. At the end of the month, based on sales records, distributors will deposit the advance tax—calculated at Tk2 per thousand—into the government treasury.
While the legal tax liability rests with the retailer, distributors will collect and deposit it on their behalf.
Arrangements are also being made to facilitate tax payments via mobile financial services (MFS).
According to NBR sources, the app will initially roll out exclusively for distributors, with plans to make its use mandatory for all wholesalers in phases.
To determine app development and implementation strategies, the NBR will soon hold discussions with the heads of sales departments from major corporations.
An NBR official, speaking on condition of anonymity, stated that distributors will ensure tax collection via the app since they are the direct users.
Therefore, gathering input from business representatives is essential.
To this end, detailed discussions will be held with them to finalize everything.
The official noted that merely building the app is not enough; unless businesses actually use it, securing tax collection will remain impossible.
Concerns among small businesses
According to industry insiders, there are currently around 7 million retail traders in the country.
Once fully implemented, this new system will bring a massive segment of retail businesses under the advance tax net.
However, the initiative has sparked anxiety among small-scale traders, who fear that compounding tax and registration requirements will drive up operational costs—costs that could ultimately trickle down to consumer prices.
Under the current fiscal year's budget, obtaining a Business Identification Number (BIN)—which is essentially a VAT registration number—has been made compulsory for small entrepreneurs and all business types to open bank accounts.
Consequently, many small business owners are forced to register for VAT just to open bank accounts.
Shafiqul Islam, a retail businessman, said: "Sales are dead. On top of that, the government is rolling out one rule after another. Retailers are facing losses and harassment."
Md Nazmul Hasan Mahmud, president of the Bangladesh Dokan Malik Samity, told Dhaka Tribune that small traders are being dragged into turnover taxes and forced to secure BINs, creating panic within the business community. Complaints are pouring in that traders cannot perform banking transactions due to a lack of BINs.
Mahmud further noted that according to VAT regulations, enterprises with an annual turnover of up to Tk35 lakh are exempt from VAT registration or BIN requirements—a point they have repeatedly raised through protests and human chains.
Highlighting the extra administrative overhead imposed on small businesses by VAT rules, he explained that a single shopkeeper is required to maintain five separate registers.
Giving an example, he cited a 100-square-foot shop where the owner works alongside two semi-literate employees. Hiring a dedicated accountant, purchasing a computer, allocating space for it, and paying the staff salary involves overhead costs that small retailers simply cannot afford.

item.title: ACME DiaCare organizes diabetes awareness run at Hatirjheel
item.description:
ACME's DiaCare organized a diabetes awareness run titled “Emlino DiaBeat Run” at Hatirjheel on November 14, marking World Diabetes Day.
Participants from different age groups and professions took part in the event, alongside members of various running communities who joined as community partners. The initiative aimed to promote diabetes awareness and encourage an active lifestyle through physical activity.
The event was organized by ACME's DiaCare, the diabetic care portfolio of pharmaceutical company The ACME Laboratories Ltd.
The event was attended by Tasneem Sinha, managing director; Sabrina Juned, deputy managing director; Motiur Rahman Sinha, director; Md Ferdous Khan, executive director (sales and distribution); Gobinda Goswami, director (sales); Mohammad Ziauddin, head of marketing; Md Humayun Kabir, executive director (international business); Dr Syed A M Mustafij Billah, executive director (plant operations); and A K M Mushiur Rahman Khan, executive director (HR and administration), along with other senior company officials.
The event was organized by ACME's DiaCare team, led by Md Mahbubur Rahman, business unit head, alongside Subrata Sarkar, group in-charge, and team members Rusat Jahin Anmol, Usaid Mostafa and Md Ishtiaque Hossain.
The initiative was based on this year's World Diabetes Day theme, “Take Early Action on Diabetes.” While discussions on diabetes often focus on managing the condition after diagnosis, the event sought to highlight the importance of prevention and reducing health risks through healthy lifestyle choices and regular physical activity.
A special awareness session was also conducted by endocrinologist Associate Professor Dr Rushda Sharmin Binte Rouf. She shared insights into diabetes prevention, the importance of timely action and maintaining a healthy lifestyle.
The session aimed to improve participants' understanding of diabetes and encourage them to adopt preventive measures early to reduce their risk.
Ahead of the main event, a “Kit Expo” and kit collection day was held on November 12 at the InterContinental Dhaka. Participants collected their official running jerseys and kit bags during the event.
A Body Mass Index (BMI) chart was also arranged as part of the initiative. Runners and visitors collecting their kits showed interest in checking their height and weight to understand their BMI.
According to the organizers, diabetes should be approached with awareness rather than fear, with preventive measures taken from the outset. Small daily habits, such as walking or running for a while, can help reduce the risk of diabetes.
Through the initiative, ACME's DiaCare reaffirmed its commitment to promoting a healthier, more active and diabetes-risk-conscious society.
The event was managed by Ultra Camp Runners (UCR).

item.title: Durbin Bangla vandalized: Owners estimate Tk30 lakh in losses
item.description:
A popular restaurant, Durbin Bangla, in Dhaka’s Mohakhali area was vandalised for nearly 30 minutes on Friday after a youth became angry when asked to wait for a table, leaving the owners with an estimated Tk25-30 lakh in losses.
The attackers allegedly assaulted several employees, smashed furniture and glass fittings, looted cash and damaged CCTV cameras before removing the recording system’s hard drive, according to the restaurant authorities.
The incident took place around 11am on Friday. The restaurant remained closed on Saturday as the owners began repair work.
Restaurant owner Shafin Baig said the trouble began when a young man arrived alone and demanded to sit at a table reserved for a family of five. A staff member asked him to wait briefly, assuring him that another seat would be arranged soon.
The youth allegedly responded, “I’ll show you who I am,” before calling others to the restaurant.
Three to four youths arrived first and assaulted an employee. More joined them, then began smashing chairs, tables, glass fittings and equipment across the restaurant, including the kitchen and waiting area. Customers fled in panic as the vandalism continued for around half an hour.
Shafin said several employees were beaten and cash was taken from the counter. He estimated the losses at Tk25-30 lakh, although the owners have yet to prepare a detailed inventory of the damaged property and missing cash.
Videos circulating on social media show a group of youths vandalising the restaurant, while police officers are seen trying to stop them. The owners said the attackers also broke CCTV cameras and took the hard drive. Police, however, said they had footage of the incident and were reviewing it to identify those involved.
The restaurant owner and some local residents alleged that the attackers were students of Government Titumir College, with some reportedly linked to a political student organisation. Shafin said he did not want to name any group and expected the police to investigate the matter.
He filed a case with Banani Police Station on Saturday evening.
The officer-in-charge of the police station, Salauddin, said police had launched an investigation and identified those involved. He said efforts were underway to arrest them and that such incidents would not be tolerated. He did not explain why no suspects had been arrested so far.
Some local residents and businesspeople believe the attack went beyond a dispute over seating, alleging that it was an attempt to exert influence and intimidate businesses in the area.
Durbin Bangla, which opened last year, had quickly gained popularity for its traditional Bengali food. According to the owners, its breakfast service regularly drew large crowds, including visitors from outside Dhaka and foreign customers. The restaurant had introduced a token system and a separate waiting area to manage the crowds.
Renovation work began on Saturday, but the owners could not say when the restaurant would reopen.
The incident has raised concerns among local businesses over the safety of employees and establishments, particularly as questions remain over how quickly those responsible will be brought to justice.

item.title: 17 AL leaders, activists held over crude bomb blasts at two courts in Jessore
item.description:
Police have arrested 17 leaders and activists of the banned Awami League over cocktail explosions at two court premises in Jessore over the past two days.
They were arrested during separate drives across eight upazilas of the district on Friday and Saturday. They were later shown arrested in a case filed under the Explosives Act and sent to jail following court orders.
The arrestees include party leaders and activists from district, upazila and union-level units.
Earlier on November 12, Sub-Inspector Raisul Islam of Kotwali Police Station filed the case under the Explosives Act, naming 21 people and several unidentified others.
Police have since been conducting special drives in the town and different upazilas to arrest those involved.
According to the case statement, around 8:50pm on Thursday, SI Raisul Islam was on duty with other police personnel in front of Jessore Railway Station when he received information about crude bomb explosions at two locations, in front of the Assistant Judge Court gate, southeast of the District and Sessions Judge Court, and behind the Chief Judicial Magistrate Court building.
Around 9pm, police visited the Assistant Judge Court premises and recovered fragments of an exploded tin container and two pieces of black adhesive tape.
Earlier, at around 8:35pm, a crude bomb had been thrown from Paris Road towards the rear of the court building. It landed inside the premises, to the right of the rear entrance, and exploded with a loud bang.
Police recovered six ball bearings, two pieces of black adhesive tape and two fragments of the exploded tin container from the spot. Police said eight people were arrested on Friday.
They are Moniruzzaman Lablu, an Awami League leader from Sujalpur village in Jessore Sadar; Lavlu, son of Abdul Majid of Bhagabatipur in Narendrapur union; Kazi Bakerul Islam Iran, son of Kazi Abdul Mannan of Chanchra Raypara; Arman Hossain Rizvi, son of Lutfur Rahman of Dharmatala; Dalim Hossain, son of the late Fazlul Haque of the area behind Bockchar L Market; Abdul Alim Gazi; Shariful Islam; and Sanowar Hossain.
On Saturday, police arrested eight more people during drives in Jhikargachha and Jessore Sadar upazilas.
They are Hriday Islam, son of the late Hafizur Islam of Shashtitala; former district Awami League member Kazi Alamgir Hossain; Jhikargachha upazila Awami League General Secretary Musa Mahmud; Awami League member Shahiduzzaman Selim; Khairuzzaman Bappy of Chanchra Raypara; former Chanchra union Jubo League General Secretary Badsha Faisal; Azizul Islam of Kholadanga; and Sohel Rana of Talbaria village.
Officer-in-Charge of Jessore Kotwali Police Station Kabir Hossain said 17 people had been arrested over the explosions at the two court premises in the past two days.
"All the arrestees are active members of the banned Awami League. They are carrying out such subversive activities to disrupt public order and destabilise Jessore. Drives are underway to arrest others involved in the incidents," he said.
He added that the arrestees had been shown arrested in the explosives case and sent to jail through court orders.
Meanwhile, apart from the two court premises, crude bombs were also exploded in front of the July Memorial in the Bakultala area of the town on Thursday night.
In a separate incident, miscreants hurled two crude bombs at the house of Shimul Hossain, education affairs secretary of the Sadar upazila BNP unit, in Chhatiantala village.
Neither of the bombs exploded. The following morning, police recovered the two unexploded crude bombs and a handwritten note from the house. The note contained a death threat against the BNP leader.
The series of explosions at different locations in the town and its outskirts on the same night triggered panic among residents.

item.title: Milon: Govt keen to boost investment in science, research
item.description:
Education Minister Dr A N M Ehsanul Hoque Milon on Saturday said the government is keen to increase investment in the education sector, particularly in science, innovation, research and development.
“Research institutions and related organizations will have to come forward in this regard,” he said while addressing a conference titled "Chemical Innovation for Future Challenge" organized by Bangladesh Chemical Society at Nabab Nawab Ali Chowdhury Senate Building of Dhaka University.
Mentioning that around Tk 5,000 crore has been allocated for the HEAT project under the University Grants Commission (UGC), he said various research and development projects are underway in the country and the government wants to invest more in science and technology, innovation and research.
Highlighting the potential of Bangladesh's human resources, Milon said the country's students and researchers have the capacity to compete at the international level. Recently, 23 scientists from the University of Dhaka have been included in the list of the world's top 2 percent scientists. This is a matter of pride for the country, he said.
However, human resources must not be kept merely as an invisible asset, and they have to be turned into productive and visible assets. For this reason, the government is also laying emphasis on increasing investment in technical education, he added.
Referring to the use of garments made from plant fibre and the need for research on the diversified use of jute, he said jute fibre is extremely important.
Yet Bangladesh has not made the expected progress in the diversified use of this resource and in increasing the variety of jute products, he said, highlighting that research must be increased to develop new products from jute fibre.
He noted that there is also scope to increase the use of eco-friendly and biodegradable jute bags.
The minister said an initiative has been taken to provide uniforms to primary school students across the country from the beginning of 2027. The government also has a plan to provide jute bags to students for carrying books and exercise books.

item.title: Cyclone Sidr still haunts elderly fishermen
item.description:
As Bangladesh prepares to mark the 19th anniversary of Cyclone Sidr, elderly fishermen in the coastal region say the 1988 cyclone was even more devastating, recalling how they lost fathers and other family members to the disaster.
Many were teenagers or young men when the cyclone struck the coastal region. Having survived successive disasters, they continue to venture into the sea, but frequent low-pressure systems and rough weather have become a growing concern.
Nurul Islam, a fisherman from Kabiraj in Raruli, said he was at Golakata Char during the 1988 cyclone. He survived by clinging to tree branches, but the force of the wind eventually snapped them, throwing him into the water. He managed to stay alive by catching hold of another large tree.
He was also at Dublar Char during Cyclone Sidr in 2007, when seven or eight members of his fishing team died. He said they had to bury the bodies in the sand. “The 1988 cyclone was far more terrifying than Sidr. Even holding on to tree branches could not save us. The memories still send shivers down my spine,” he said.
Shankar Kumar Bihari, a fisherman from Hetampur in Paikgachha, lost his father, Goshto Bihari, in the 1988 cyclone. He was a school student at the time and had accompanied his father to a fair after his examinations.
“The next morning, bodies were scattered everywhere. We found a sack of wet rice and shared it among 30 to 35 people. It was an unimaginable disaster,” he recalled.
Many families affected by Sidr are yet to recover from the devastation.
Jalil Fakir, 38, of Bhaijora village in Morelganj, has been living with his wife and son in a dilapidated house with a golpata roof covered in polythene since losing his home to Sidr. Despite working as a hired fisherman for 27 years, he cannot afford to build a new house.
His wife, Reshma Begum, said rainwater enters their home during storms, soaking their bedding and clothes and forcing the family to spend sleepless nights.
In Southkhali, Sharan Khola, more than 100 families affected by Sidr and subsequent cyclones are still living on embankments, said former union parishad member Zakir Hossain.
He said repeated disasters, including Cyclone Amphan, had prevented residents from rebuilding their lives. Although an embankment has been constructed, inadequate river management continues to leave the area vulnerable.
Zakir also lost his father and nephew to Sidr. Despite 19 years of struggle, he said, his family has been unable to rebuild the house they lost.
On November 15, 2007, Sidr struck the southwestern coast, bringing a storm surge of 12-15 feet and devastating coastal areas of Satkhira, Khulna, Bagerhat, Barguna and Patuakhali. Southkhali was among the worst-hit areas, with 778 people killed.
Official figures put the nationwide death toll at 3,363, while the Red Crescent estimated it at around 10,000. The cyclone affected 30 districts and 200 upazilas, destroying homes, roads, bridges, embankments and agricultural land and leaving thousands of families struggling to rebuild their lives.

item.title: DSCC aims to make Dhaka a model city
item.description:
Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) aims to transform the capital into a model city through efforts to make it cleaner, greener and more peaceful, with a focus on improving the overall urban environment.
DSCC Administrator Md Abdus Salam said he wants to establish Dhaka as a model of development by turning this vision into reality.
He said the corporation's cleanliness campaign would continue until the capital was clean.
He made the remarks on Saturday while speaking at a cleanliness and mosquito-control drive organized on Bailey Road in the capital as part of the DSCC's weekly Cleaning Day program.
The DSCC administrator said: “Since taking responsibility, I have been trying to bring the Dhaka city corporation closer to the people. At the same time, I want to establish an accountable system for the public. Various activities are being carried out every day toward that goal.”
Outlining plans to develop Bailey Road as a specially designated clean road, he said the entire stretch from one end of the road to Shantinagar intersection would be declared a special road. The initiative would be expanded later, he added.
He said the road would be kept clean, with no garbage allowed to accumulate anywhere along the stretch.
Abdus Salam said discussions had already been held with Bailey Road residents, adding that a separate cleanliness campaign would be organized with their participation.
Initiatives would also be taken to plant trees in the area and keep the sidewalks clean, he said.
The DSCC administrator said keeping Dhaka clean was essential to protecting residents from mosquito infestations and dengue. Similarly, protecting the city from air pollution would be difficult without maintaining cleanliness.
“There is no alternative to keeping Dhaka clean, beautiful, green and pollution-free if we want to live healthy lives,” he said.
Seeking cooperation from city residents, Abdus Salam urged people not to dump garbage indiscriminately. He particularly called on business owners to keep the areas in front of their establishments clean.
“Garbage collected while cleaning shops must not be dumped on the streets. It must be disposed of at designated locations,” he said.
He also urged conscious citizens and local volunteers to contribute to cleanliness activities, calling on people across all wards and neighborhoods to participate in the campaign.
He said residents should monitor whether garbage was being dumped illegally and whether the city corporation was collecting waste properly. They should also inform the corporation if mosquito infestations were found in any area and check whether mosquito-control chemicals were being sprayed.
He added that everyone should stand beside the public to ensure citizens received the necessary services and facilities.
“We believe that one day Dhaka will become a beautiful and peaceful city. It will be developed as a model of development and gain recognition worldwide as a beautiful city befitting the capital of Bangladesh,” he said.
The DSCC chief executive officer, chief waste management officer, chief health officer and other officials, along with local dignitaries and volunteers, were present at the event.
As part of Cleaning Day, special cleanliness and mosquito-control drives, along with public awareness activities, were also conducted across all 75 wards under the leadership of the corporation's regional executive officers.

item.title: India edge Bhutan to reach SAFF Championship final
item.description:
Defending champions India booked their place in the SAFF Championship 2026 final after edging past Bhutan 2-1 in the first semifinal at the National Stadium in Dhaka on Saturday.
PV Vishnu and captain Chinglensana Singh scored in the first half to put India in control, but Bhutan mounted a spirited fightback after the break to make it a nervy finish.
India took the lead in the eighth minute when Khaiminthang Lhungdim's long diagonal pass found East Bengal forward Vishnu on the left side of the box. After controlling the ball and shifting onto his right foot, Vishnu calmly slotted it into the bottom-right corner.
The defending champions doubled their advantage in the 28th minute. Manglenthang Kipgen's corner caused confusion in the Bhutanese defence, allowing Chinglensana to collect the loose ball and fire home from close range.
India went into the interval with a two-goal cushion, having largely dominated the first half. However, Bhutan returned with renewed determination and pulled one back just three minutes after the restart.
A long free-kick delivery created chaos inside the Indian penalty area, with Chencho Gyeltshen's effort from the left redirected towards goal by Kinzang Tobden, who headed into an unguarded net. The assistant referee initially flagged for offside, but a VAR review overturned the decision and the goal was allowed to stand.
VAR was again at the centre of attention in the 65th minute when India were awarded a penalty after substitute Irfan's cross struck Nima Wangdi's hand. However, the referee reversed the decision following an on-field review.
India came close to sealing the victory in the 85th minute when Suhail Bhat produced an impressive solo run before unleashing a right-footed effort that struck the crossbar.
Bhutan continued to search for an equaliser, but India held on to secure their place in the final and keep their hopes of a record-extending 10th SAFF title alive.
The match also marked the first use of the Video Assistant Referee (VAR) system in the history of the competition.
India, who topped Group B with victories over Pakistan (3-2) and the Maldives (1-0), have now reached the final for the 14th time in 15 appearances. They have won the championship nine times and finished runners-up on four occasions.
Naushad Moosa's side will face either hosts Bangladesh or Pakistan in the November 17 final.
Bhutan, meanwhile, bowed out after finishing second in Group A. They began their campaign with a 1-0 defeat to Bangladesh before drawing 2-2 with Sri Lanka to advance to the semifinals on goal difference.

item.title: Six held over deadly Turkiye steel blast that killed 17
item.description:
Six people were arrested overnight after a huge blast at a steel plant near the western city of Izmir killed 17 workers, with grieving families waiting Tuesday to receive their loved ones’ bodies for burial.
Onlookers said Monday’s massive explosion felt like “an earthquake” when it ripped through the HABAS steel factory in Aliaga, a district 60 kilometers (37 miles) north of Izmir known for shipbreaking and heavy industry.
Police have so far detained six people in connection with the incident, with Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar warning “the number could rise.”
The deadly blast at one of Turkiye’s top steel producers also left around a dozen people injured, at least one in critical condition.
Outside the forensic institute in Aliaga, bereaved family members told AFP they had been waiting all night for confirmation that their loved ones had been identified so they could be laid to rest.
“We have been here since yesterday, we’re waiting for the DNA results. Since the bodies are in a condition that makes visual identification impossible, the identification process is carried out through DNA analysis,” said Turgut Dilek, saying his nephew Ozcan Efe was one of the dead.
Meanwhile, there was no word on the fate of a 40-year-old man who set himself alight outside the factory on Monday evening and was taken to hospital with severe injuries, IHA news agency said.
The man had worked for years as a truck driver at the factory, IHA said, without mention of earlier reports that his brother had died in the blast.
Workers’ groups have accused Habas of a chequered safety record, and President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on Monday vowed that investigators would get to the bottom of what happened.
Turkiye’s pro-Kurdish DEM party -- which said late Monday “not a single party must go unpunished” at the factory -- sent a delegation to visit the families and the injured on Tuesday led by its co-chair Tulay Hatimogullari.
Jailed Istanbul mayor Ekrem Imamoglu, Erdogan’s chief political rival, also demanded accountability.
“Workplace deaths are not fate. The causes of the accident must be fully established, and anyone who was negligent or at fault must be held accountable,” he wrote on X.
Izmir governor Suleyman Elban said the explosion happened during “a boiler replacement operation.”
Contacted by AFP, Habas declined to respond to any questions.
On Monday, police detained two representatives of a workers’ collective outside Aliaga hospital while trying to make a statement about workplace safety issues, a spokesman told AFP.
Workers’ groups have called a protest in Aliaga on Tuesday, saying: “STOP this hell of exploitation in which dozens of our comrades have died and hundreds were left disabled because of employers’ greed!”

item.title: US air travel resumption will ‘take time’ after hours-long stop
item.description:
Flights in the United States resumed on Saturday after being grounded for several hours due to a major communications outage, though authorities said returning to normal operations would take time.
The nationwide stop on Friday sparked widespread chaos and left hundreds of thousands of passengers in limbo, with some pulled off planes moments before departure by airline staff who appeared in the dark about unfolding events.
The incident marked only the second time such an alert had been issued in US airspace -- which is among the busiest in the world -- since the 9/11 attacks.
The ground stop lasted around four hours and was lifted at 8:15pm Eastern Time (0115 GMT Saturday).
Federal Aviation Administration officials reopened the airspace on Friday night “after restoring full functionality” at air traffic control facilities, according to Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy.
“It will take us time (to) resume normal operations... Our top priority is the safety of you and your family when you fly,” Duffy said.
Administration officials blamed the incident on telecommunications issues with decades-old equipment, adding there was no evidence of foul play.
“This is a legacy system problem,” Duffy said. “We have old, old switches, old routers.
“We use 1980s little copper lines. It’s an old system that went down, and went down everywhere. It got overloaded.”
Duffy had formally asked Congress on Thursday for $30.1 billion in funds to upgrade and modernize the air traffic control System.
As the ground stop was lifted, he repeated his plea.
“I’m going to say it a million times: the Congress has to give the resources to the president so he can finish this bill,” he said.
There were almost 6,000 flights canceled, including some international routes, according to FlightAware, a tracking platform.
Footage from airports around the country showed gates full, with planes waiting on taxiways.
Passengers thronged concourses, desperate for information about an outage that had thrown their plans into chaos.
“We’re trying to debate whether or not we need to reschedule or drive or what, but if the whole country is stopped, that means the highways are going to be jammed too,” said Joseph Anderson, 72, who was trying to fly from Las Vegas to Oakland, California.
A nationwide ground stop is highly unusual.
There was one such stop in January 2023 when a pilot notification system failed, but the only other national stop happened in the wake of the 9/11 attacks in September 2001, when no aircraft took to the skies for days.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin stressed there was no evidence of any hostile action on Friday.
“We’ve seen zero evidence that this was a cyberattack or (AI) attack,” he told a news conference.
He also ruled out any connection with the outage that affected Microsoft this week, knocking email systems offline for millions of users, public services and businesses worldwide.
The stop caused misery at airports around the country.
At New York’s LaGuardia Airport, Tiara Johnson said she had been trying to get to Orlando for a concert with a friend.
“They just keep delaying it... So it started out at 7:55. Then it went to 8:30, 9:30. Now it’s at 10:30. So we don’t know when it’s gonna leave,” she told AFP.
“I feel very frustrated because you know, you come to the airport and then all of a sudden your whole plans have changed and you don’t know when you’re leaving. We’re kind of stuck.”
Some travelers said they had been told their flight was delayed because of wind, while others were left to gather what information they could.
Boards at the airport continued to show departures leaving as normal, while mobile boarding passes held by those stuck on the ground appeared to show their flight was underway.
Stranded passengers were scrambling to find alternatives, with long lines forming at rental car counters at the airport in Las Vegas.
Susan Sardina said she had boarded her flight back to Orange County, California when staff told passengers there was a problem.
“We were already on our flight to leave and we were told to get off,” she told AFP as she stood in a lengthy queue for a rental car.
For those looking on the bright side, the delay was a chance to extend a break.
Kathy Sommers was on her way home from visiting friends in Las Vegas when her flight got canceled.
“We’re blessed that our friends are coming back to pick us up,” she said. “So one more night to play cards.”

item.title: 69 primary schools running without headteachers in Sariakandi
item.description:
As many as 69 of the 168 government primary schools in Bogra’s Sariakandi upazila are operating without regular headteachers, with acting headteachers overseeing their activities.
The shortage has created administrative challenges and placed additional pressure on teachers, prompting calls for the immediate appointment of headteachers.
According to the upazila education office, 54 schools have headteachers serving in their regular posts, while 45 have teachers performing the duties of headteachers on an additional charge basis. The remaining 69 schools are being run by acting headteachers.
Asaduzzaman, headteacher of Antarpara Government Primary School, said he had been serving in an acting capacity for several years, making it difficult to manage both teaching and administrative responsibilities.
“We have to take our regular classes while handling administrative work and maintaining communication with guardians. When we have to visit the upazila headquarters for official duties, other teachers have to take additional classes,” he said, calling for an early resolution.
Sariakandi Upazila Education Officer Sheikh Mahtabur Rahman said the issue had been brought to the attention of higher authorities.
He said acting headteachers would soon be formally appointed, followed by the recruitment of assistant teachers against vacant posts.
However, he claimed that the absence of regular headteachers had not disrupted classroom teaching or caused any learning gaps among students.

item.title: GST cluster may add 4 universities, up to 550 seats
item.description:
The number of undergraduate seats at public universities under the General, Science and Technology (GST) admission cluster may increase in the 2026-27 academic year, with 4 additional universities potentially joining the system.
Currently, 20 universities under the cluster offer a total of 16,093 seats. If the 4 proposed universities are included, the total could rise to 16,643, adding up to 550 seats.
Updated information on undergraduate admission seats at public and private universities for the 2026-27 academic year was published on November 1. According to the data, the existing 20 GST universities have 16,093 seats.
However, the inclusion of the 4 additional universities has not yet been finalized and requires approval from the University Grants Commission (UGC).
According to the published data, the seat allocation across the 20 universities is as follows:
Islamic University has 2,515 seats; Jatiya Kabi Kazi Nazrul Islam University 1,175; Begum Rokeya University 1,395; University of Barishal 1,570; Rabindra University 850; Netrokona University 390; and Kishoreganj University 126.
Among the science and technology universities, Mawlana Bhashani Science and Technology University has 875 seats; Noakhali Science and Technology University 1,611; Jashore University of Science and Technology 1,030; Pabna University of Science and Technology 830; Gopalganj Science and Technology University 1,580; Rangamati Science and Technology University 190; and Jamalpur Science and Technology University 204.
Patuakhali Science and Technology University has 950 seats; Chandpur Science and Technology University 90; Bangladesh University of Frontier Technology 220; Sunamganj Science and Technology University 172; Pirojpur Science and Technology University 160; and Naogaon University 160.
The 4 universities being considered for inclusion are Bogura University, Thakurgaon University, Lakshmipur Science and Technology University and Meherpur University.
Meherpur University is expected to receive final approval for its Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) and English departments. If approved, the university may initially offer 80 to 100 seats.
Bogura University, Thakurgaon University and Lakshmipur Science and Technology University have yet to receive approval for their academic departments. Their seat numbers will be finalized after departmental approvals and the necessary decisions by the UGC.
Initially, each of these 3 universities may offer around 100 to 150 seats. Together, the 4 institutions could add an estimated 380 to 550 seats to the GST cluster.
The UGC decided to introduce the cluster-based admission system at public universities from the 2020-21 academic year to reduce the financial and logistical burden on students.
The system was designed to spare applicants the expense and inconvenience of sitting separate admission tests at multiple universities. Through a single coordinated admission test, students can compete for seats at several participating institutions.
Preparations are also underway to continue the system for the 2026-27 academic year. However, whether the 4 additional universities will join and how many seats they will offer will depend on departmental approvals and the UGC's final decisions.

item.title: IUBAT professor elected chairman of IEB Dhaka centre
item.description:
Professor Engr Dr Monirul Islam, chairman of the Department of Civil Engineering at the International University of Business Agriculture and Technology (IUBAT), has been elected chairman of the Dhaka Centre of the Institution of Engineers, Bangladesh (IEB) for the 2027–2028 term.
The election was held on Thursday, November 12, 2026, in Dhaka and other centers across the country, with engineers voting directly to elect their representatives. Dr Islam will serve a two-year term.
Dr Islam is an engineer, educator and researcher with extensive experience in engineering education and professional development. He previously served as dean of IUBAT’s College of Engineering and Technology, where he led efforts to strengthen academic programs and research activities.
During his tenure, all four engineering programs at IUBAT — Civil Engineering, Computer Science and Engineering, Electrical and Electronic Engineering, and Mechanical Engineering — received six-year accreditation from the Board of Accreditation for Engineering and Technical Education (BAETE) under the Outcome-Based Education (OBE) framework.
As chairman of the Department of Civil Engineering, he oversees academic programs and works to improve teaching quality, research opportunities and students’ professional skills.
The IEB is the country's oldest and largest professional organization for engineers. It works to advance engineering education, technological development and professional standards while promoting collaboration among engineers. The Dhaka Centre regularly organizes professional training, seminars, research activities and policy discussions.
IUBAT has congratulated Dr Islam on his election, describing the achievement as recognition of the university's contribution to engineering education and the profession.
Inspired by the vision of its founder, Professor Dr M Alimullah Miyan, IUBAT has continued to focus on higher education, research and skilled human resource development. The university expressed hope that Dr Islam's leadership would strengthen the IEB Dhaka Centre, promote engineering excellence and encourage research and innovation for the country's sustainable development.

item.title: Winter fatigue: The surprising reasons you're always tired despite sleeping more
item.description:
As winter arrives, many people find themselves sleeping longer than usual yet waking up feeling tired. Despite getting enough rest, daytime drowsiness, low energy, and difficulty concentrating can become common complaints.
However, cold weather alone is not responsible. Reduced daylight, changes in the body's biological clock, and seasonal lifestyle habits can all contribute to winter fatigue.
The body's internal clock, known as the circadian rhythm, regulates sleep and wakefulness. During winter, shorter days and reduced sunlight exposure can disrupt this natural cycle by affecting melatonin, the hormone responsible for regulating sleep.
This may leave people feeling sleepy, sluggish, and less alert throughout the day.
Cold weather often discourages outdoor activities and exercise. Spending more time indoors and being less physically active can increase feelings of tiredness.
Dietary changes may also play a role. Heavier meals, irregular eating habits, and inadequate water intake can contribute to fatigue. Since people tend to feel less thirsty in winter, dehydration can easily go unnoticed.
Persistent tiredness is not always seasonal. Anaemia, thyroid disorders, vitamin B12 or vitamin D deficiency, diabetes, and sleep disorders can also cause prolonged fatigue.
In some cases, reduced sunlight may contribute to seasonal affective disorder (SAD), a form of depression associated with changes in mood, sleep and energy levels.
According to physicians, maintaining a regular sleep schedule, spending time outdoors in daylight, exercising regularly, and following a balanced diet can help improve energy levels.
Staying adequately hydrated and ensuring good-quality sleep are equally important.
However, if fatigue continues despite sufficient rest, medical advice should be sought, particularly when accompanied by unexplained weight changes, dizziness, breathing difficulties, or persistent low mood.
While occasional winter sluggishness is common, prolonged exhaustion should never be dismissed as simply a seasonal effect.

item.title: The truth about hair oils and hair growth
item.description:
For generations, people have relied on different types of hair oils to combat dryness, breakage, hair loss, and baldness. However, experts say there is little strong scientific evidence that applying oil to the scalp directly accelerates hair growth.
Hair growth begins in the hair follicles beneath the scalp and is influenced by genetics, hormones, nutrition, and overall health.
Although oils cannot necessarily stimulate faster growth, they can help retain moisture, reduce friction, and protect hair from damage and breakage.
Different oils offer different benefits depending on hair type and condition. Some may be particularly helpful for dry, damaged, or brittle hair.
1. Coconut oil
Research suggests that coconut oil can reduce protein loss from hair, helping protect it against damage and breakage. It may be particularly beneficial for dry and damaged hair.
2. Argan oil
Argan oil helps smooth frizzy hair, reduce dryness, and improve manageability, leaving hair feeling softer and looking shinier.
3. Almond oil
Almond oil can help retain moisture and make hair easier to detangle. However, scientific evidence supporting its ability to promote hair growth remains limited.
4. Rosemary oil
Some preliminary studies suggest that rosemary oil may have potential benefits for certain types of hair loss, although further research is needed to establish its effectiveness.
Experts recommend diluting rosemary essential oil with a suitable carrier oil before applying it to the scalp to reduce the risk of irritation.
5. Castor oil
Castor oil is widely used because of the belief that it promotes thicker and longer hair. However, there is no strong scientific evidence that it directly stimulates new hair growth.
Experts say there is no universal rule for applying hair oil, as scalp conditions and hair types vary from person to person.
For some people, applying oil once or twice a week before washing may be beneficial. Leaving oil on overnight is not necessary, and skipping oil treatments does not automatically damage hair.
Frequent use of hair dryers, straighteners, and curling irons can weaken hair, increase dryness, and cause breakage. While oils may improve softness and reduce friction, they do not provide complete protection against heat damage.
Experts recommend using specially formulated heat-protection products, avoiding excessively high temperatures, and gently detangling wet hair.
Experts emphasize that hair loss and hair breakage are two different problems. Breakage often results from excessive heat styling, chemical treatments, rough brushing, or improper hair care.
Hair loss, on the other hand, may be linked to genetics, hormonal changes, illness, stress, medication, or nutritional deficiencies.
Persistent hair loss, sudden excessive shedding, or scalp symptoms such as itching, redness, and inflammation should be assessed by a dermatologist.
Simply applying hair oil cannot address the underlying causes of these conditions.
A balanced diet containing adequate protein, iron, and other essential nutrients plays an important role in maintaining healthy hair. Experts also recommend getting sufficient sleep, managing stress, and handling hair gently to minimize unnecessary damage.
Hair-growth supplements should not be taken without medical advice, particularly when there is no confirmed nutritional deficiency.
Although hair oils can improve softness, manageability, and protection against breakage, experts caution that no oil should be considered a guaranteed solution for faster hair growth.

item.title: NEIR without tax reform risks deepening digital divide
item.description:
Bangladesh is preparing to roll out the National Equipment Identity Register (NEIR), a long-overdue system designed to curb the import and use of illegal mobile phones, protect government revenue, and bring order to a market that has long operated in the shadows.
The intent is sound. The timing, however, raises a question that policymakers would do well to answer before January 2027 arrives: if smartphones remain among the most heavily taxed consumer goods in the country, who exactly will NEIR bring into the formal market?
The numbers tell a troubling story. Bangladesh currently imposes a combined tax burden of 64.25% on imported smartphones, one of the highest in the region.
Sri Lanka charges zero customs duty on smartphones. Nepal charges 13%. Pakistan's total duty burden, though recently reduced, remains a fraction of Bangladesh's.
Yet Bangladesh, a country that aspires to build a digitally inclusive economy, taxes a smartphone at a rate that adds over Tk60,000 in duties alone on a device assessed at Tk1 lakh.
The result is predictable.
Consumers who cannot afford the official price or who simply recognize the arbitrage turn to the grey market.
In 2026, unofficial smartphone sales are estimated to have risen 25% over the previous year, while official sales fell by nearly 17%.
The government lost an estimated Tk6,425 crore in revenue from that informal market alone.
These are not the numbers of a system working as intended.
NEIR, in theory, should change this calculus.
By blocking unregistered devices from accessing mobile networks, the system removes the primary utility of a grey market phone.
But this logic only holds if the official market offers a viable alternative.
At present, it does not, not at current prices, not in a year when the IMF projects Bangladesh's inflation at 10.9% and global memory chipset prices show no sign of declining.
Implementing NEIR while keeping the existing duty structure intact does not simply fail to solve the grey market problem; it actively worsens it.
When official phones become more expensive and grey market phones get blocked, consumers do not disappear; they find another way. Some will travel.
Some will carry phones in through personal baggage allowances.
Some will simply defer the purchase entirely, which may be the worst outcome of all for a country where smartphone penetration stands at just 45%, a figure that lags far behind Nepal at 73%, Pakistan at 72%, and Nigeria at 75%, all countries with lower per capita incomes than Bangladesh.
That last comparison deserves more attention than it typically receives.
The standard defense of high smartphone tariffs is that they protect domestic manufacturing and generate revenue.
Both arguments have merit in isolation, but neither holds up well against the evidence.
The revenue argument is weaker still: a tax so high that it drives consumers into an unregistered grey market does not maximize revenue; it simply relocates the transaction beyond the government's reach.
The Tk6,425 crore in estimated annual revenue loss from informal sales is not an abstract figure.
It represents the direct fiscal cost of a duty structure that prioritizes the appearance of protection over the reality of collection.
What Bangladesh needs is not a choice between NEIR and lower duties, but both, implemented together.
Reducing customs duty from 25% to 5% and eliminating the regulatory duty entirely, bringing the total tax burden closer to 33%, would not undermine domestic producers.
Domestic manufacturers retain a significant cost advantage even under a rationalized import duty structure, as the gap between locally assembled devices and fully imported ones, accounting for shipping costs, would remain between 12 and 23 percentage points in favor of local production.
It would, however, make official channels meaningfully competitive with informal ones, give NEIR a market it can actually serve, and begin to close the smartphone penetration gap that is quietly widening Bangladesh's digital divide.
Every percentage point of that gap represents households, students, freelancers, and small business owners unable to access the digital economy on its own terms.
Bangladesh has articulated ambitious targets for digital transformation.
Achieving them requires a population that can actually afford the device through which that transformation happens.
A registration system that locks out grey market phones while keeping official prices out of reach does not advance that goal.
It simply moves the barrier from one side of the border to the other.
The more consequential reform, the one that would actually expand the formal market, grow government revenue, and accelerate digital inclusion, is the one being treated as secondary.
It should be first.
Md Abbas worked as a journalist for more than a decade, covering different issues including the rights of marginalized communities, and overseas employment and migration

item.title: Why some people struggle to enjoy their holidays
item.description:
A holiday is meant to offer a break from the pressures of everyday life. Yet, for some people, time away from work and routine brings little relief. Instead of returning refreshed, they find themselves just as tired, or even more stressed, than before they left.
The problem may have less to do with the destination and more to do with how people approach their time off, according to Dr Chandni Tugnait, an Indian psychotherapist and founder and director of Gateway of Healing.
In an interview with Hindustan Times, Tugnait identified several psychological factors that can prevent people from enjoying their holidays.
Checking emails over breakfast or answering a quick call from a hotel room may seem harmless, but such habits keep the mind connected to workplace demands. Some people also feel guilty about being away or worry that things will go wrong in their absence, making it difficult to switch off.
A packed itinerary can turn a holiday into a race against time. Trying to visit every popular attraction, café and landmark often means waking up early, rushing through meals and spending much of the day travelling between places. Rather than relaxing, holidaymakers end up working through a checklist.
After months of anticipation, people may build an ideal picture of how their holiday should unfold. Unexpected rain, disappointing accommodation or disagreements among travel companions can then feel like major setbacks, overshadowing the rest of the trip.
The pressure to capture the perfect photograph for social media can also take people away from the experience itself. As Tugnait noted, spending too much time framing pictures and thinking about how a post will look can prevent travellers from being fully present in the moment.
For some, thoughts of unfinished tasks and mounting work begin to creep in before the holiday is even over. Anxiety about returning to daily responsibilities can take away from the final days of the break.
Enjoying a holiday does not necessarily depend on choosing the right destination or visiting more places. Keeping plans flexible, setting firm boundaries around work and accepting that not everything will go as expected can make time away more rewarding.
Allowing room for unplanned moments, rather than trying to make every day perfect, may help travellers return home feeling genuinely rested.

item.title: Dengue cases rise in Faridpur
item.description:
Dengue cases continue to rise in Faridpur, with 44 new patients admitted to hospitals in the district on Saturday.
According to official figures, 2,173 people have received treatment for dengue at government hospitals in the district so far. Currently, 132 patients are undergoing treatment, while 10 people have died from the disease.
Private hospitals are also reporting daily admissions of dengue patients.
Meanwhile, the district administration and Faridpur Municipality have stepped up mosquito-control drives across the town. Fogger machines are being used to spray mosquito-killing chemicals in drains, residential areas and surrounding neighborhoods.
Faridpur Civil Surgeon Dr Mahmudul Hasan said all necessary measures were being taken to ensure treatment for dengue patients in line with government directives.
However, he stressed that government initiatives alone could not prevent the spread of the disease. He urged residents to ensure that water does not accumulate in their homes or surrounding areas.
Faridpur Municipality Administrator Md Ilyasur Rahman said mosquito-control activities were being conducted in phases across all 27 wards, using both government allocations and municipal funds.
He urged residents to remain vigilant and take preventive measures at home, saying public awareness and collective efforts were essential to containing the outbreak.

item.title: Bangladesh, Singapore sign MoU on carbon market cooperation
item.description:
Bangladesh and Singapore have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to enhance cooperation in international carbon markets under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, opening up new opportunities for climate financing and joint initiatives to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
The MoU was signed this morning at the Singapore Pavilion on the sidelines of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkiye, said to a press release.
State Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shaikh Faridul Islam signed the agreement on behalf of Bangladesh, while Secretary of Singapore's Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment Melvin Ong signed for his country.
The agreement is expected to facilitate Bangladesh's participation in international carbon markets, expand access to carbon financing and environmentally sustainable investments, and support the implementation of the country's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC 3.0).
Speaking at the signing ceremony, Faridul Islam said Bangladesh warmly welcomes the partnership with Singapore under the Paris Agreement.
He said the cooperation would help unlock new opportunities for carbon finance, develop high-quality and transparent carbon markets, and advance the implementation of Bangladesh's NDC 3.0.
Bangladesh is committed to working closely with Singapore to promote sustainable development, achieve ambitious climate goals and strengthen effective global climate action, he added.
Under the MoU, the two countries will exchange information, knowledge and experience on carbon credits and explore further cooperation in greenhouse gas emission reduction projects based on mutual interests and benefits.
The partnership is expected to accelerate climate change mitigation efforts by utilizing the opportunities for international cooperation provided under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement.
It is also expected to support the development of internationally recognized carbon markets in Bangladesh, facilitate the transfer of climate-friendly technologies, attract greater private sector investment and create new avenues for international climate finance.
The initiative will further contribute to Bangladesh's transition towards sustainable and low-carbon development and help achieve its national climate targets.
